articles.title: Hybrid and Higher-Order Inflammasome Assemblies in Innate Immunity: The Case of Superinflammasomes.
articles.abstract: Inflammasomes are classically understood as canonical complexes assembled around individual cytosolic sensors, such as NLRP3, NLRP1, NLRC4, AIM2, or Pyrin. This view has been highly productive, but accumulating evidence suggests that it may be incomplete. Several reports now support physical or functional cooperation between distinct innate immune receptors, including NLRC4-NLRP3 co-recruitment, NLRP3-dependent licensing by NLRP11, inhibitory interaction between NLRP12 and NLRP3, and cooperation between NOD2 and NLRP1. More recently, biochemical, structural and functional evidence has supported the existence of a hybrid NLRP1-NLRP3 inflammasome in human macrophages and monocytes, with additional support from clinical samples from patients with inflammasomopathies and kidney transplantation. Here, we argue that these findings fit within a broader conceptual framework in which inflammasome sensors form higher-order supramolecular assemblies, or superinflammasomes, conceptually analogous to mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes. We propose that this organizational layer may enable signal integration, amplification, kinetic tuning, structural plasticity, and inflammatory persistence in disease. This perspective calls for revising the one-sensor-one-inflammasome paradigm and suggests new opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Sympathetic neuroeffector remodeling and cardiomyocyte ferroptosis in heart failure: A stage- and compartment-specific framework for β-adrenergic/cAMP signaling.
articles.abstract: Heart failure is characterized by sympathetic remodeling, altered myocardial adrenergic responsiveness, and cardiomyocyte injury, with ferroptosis emerging as a potential contributor to adverse cardiac remodeling. This review proposes a dynamic "sympathetic-ferroptosis continuum" within a "nerve terminal-cardiomyocyte" dual-compartment framework linking cardiac sympathetic dysfunction, β1-adrenergic receptor (β1-AR)/cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling, and cardiomyocyte ferroptosis susceptibility. Sustained sympathetic drive can coexist with altered norepinephrine (NE) homeostasis at cardiac nerve terminals and myocardial β1-AR desensitization, creating a functional mismatch between sympathetic activity and myocardial signaling responsiveness. At sympathetic nerve terminals, altered β1-AR/cAMP signaling may influence tyrosine hydroxylase-dependent NE synthesis and synapsin 1/RIM1α-associated vesicle mobilization and release, alongside changes in NE transporter-mediated reuptake. In cardiomyocytes, dysregulated compartment-specific cAMP signaling may affect YAP-associated iron homeostasis, LPCAT3-mediated phospholipid remodeling, SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4-dependent antioxidant defenses, and NOX4-related oxidative stress, thereby modifying ferroptosis susceptibility. Together, these pathways provide an integrated mechanistic framework linking neurocardiac signaling imbalance with cardiomyocyte ferroptosis susceptibility. This framework identifies potential targets for preserving adaptive cAMP signaling, improving sympathetic neurotransmitter homeostasis, and limiting ferroptosis-related injury, providing new directions for compartment-specific cardioprotective strategies in heart failure.

articles.title: Resistance of digestive system malignancies to Claudin 18.2-targeting therapy: Mechanistic heterogeneity, tumor ecosystem remodeling, and rational precision strategies.
articles.abstract: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a promising therapeutic target for gastric, gastroesophageal junction (GEJ), and pancreatic cancers, with CLDN18.2-targeting agents yielding encouraging clinical outcomes; however, intrinsic and acquired drug resistance is still a key obstacle limiting long-term clinical benefits and disease control. The intricate molecular mechanisms underlying resistance have not yet been fully elucidated, and clinically feasible strategies to reverse it are urgently needed. This review establishes a five-tiered resistance framework (dysregulated expression and aberrant subcellular localization of CLDN18.2, metabolic reprogramming, intracellular bypass signaling compensation, tumor microenvironment [TME] remodeling, and immune evasion) to summarize previously fragmented resistance mechanisms. It also elucidates newly discovered core resistance mechanisms: O-GlcNAc glycosylation-induced cytoplasmic retention of CLDN18.2, trogocytosis-mediated transfer of cell membrane CLDN18.2 (mem-CLDN18.2) from tumor cells to cluster of differentiation (CD)8+ T cells, and spatial intratumoral heterogeneity-related target loss. Furthermore, it compares distinct resistance profiles across diverse therapeutic modalities and summarizes validated and emerging predictive biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI)-based risk assessment models, and clinical advances involving the use of novel agents and rational combination regimens to overcome resistance. It also comprehensively synthesizes cutting-edge findings on CLDN18.2-targeting drug resistance, forming an integrated system covering mechanisms, biomarkers, and translational strategies. This review could offer a theoretical reference for overcoming clinical drug resistance, improving the precision treatment of digestive system malignancies, and promoting the research and development of next-generation CLDN18.2-targeting drugs.

articles.title: The expansion of kinase drug discovery: new targets, platforms and indications.
articles.abstract: In the past 25 years, kinase drug discovery has grown into one of the most thriving areas in pharmaceutical research and development. What began as a field dominated by ATP-competitive small molecules has diversified into a broad therapeutic landscape that includes allosteric and covalent inhibitors, activators, proximity-induced modulators, targeted protein degraders and antibody-based therapies, with more than 150 regulatory approvals so far worldwide. In this Review, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the current kinase therapeutic landscape, including more than 2,100 kinase-targeting agents that have entered clinical development in more than 23,000 clinical trials. We cover drug platforms, new targeting approaches, the expanding target spectrum, approvals and clinical trends. Nearly half of the canonical human protein kinases have at least one clinical-stage agent, placing kinases among the most intensively explored drug target classes. Nevertheless, development remains highly concentrated around a small set of blockbuster kinase targets, such as EGFR. We also examine the features associated with successful kinase-targeting agents and causes of agent discontinuations and regulatory withdrawal.

articles.title: A miR-221-3p-CDKN1B-CDK4/β-catenin axis couples tumor progression with response to CDK4/6 inhibition in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Dysregulation of cell cycle control contributes to the progression and therapeutic resistance of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), yet the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that the cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitor Dalpiciclib suppresses ICC progression, although its efficacy varies across patient-derived models. Mechanistically, Dalpiciclib inhibits CDK4-mediated phosphorylation of β-catenin at Ser675, thereby attenuating epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastatic phenotypes. We further identify miR-221-3p as a key post-transcriptional regulator of CDK4 signaling that modulates both ICC progression and sensitivity to dalpiciclib. Elevated miR-221-3p promotes CDKN1B downregulation, thereby relieving its inhibitory effect on CDK4, enhancing β-catenin phosphorylation, and facilitating metastatic progression. Notably, circulating miR-221-3p levels closely mirrored intratumoral miR-221-3p expression and were associated with Dalpiciclib sensitivity in corresponding patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, suggesting its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for assessing treatment response. Collectively, these findings identify a miR-221-3p/CDKN1B/CDK4/β-catenin axis that links cell cycle regulation ICC progression and CDK4 inhibitor response, providing a mechanistic rationale for preclinical evaluation of Dalpiciclib treatment in ICC.

articles.title: Caspase-5 couples the cleavage of endosomal Cav1.2-C terminus to cytosolic LPS release and barrier dysfunction in colitis.
articles.abstract: Gram-negative bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) deliver lipopolysaccharide (LPS) into intestinal epithelial cells to drive ulcerative colitis (UC) progression, yet the precise mechanisms orchestrating cytosolic LPS release and subsequent pathogenic signaling remain elusive. Here, we identify a non-canonical, caspase-5-dependent signaling axis that couples endosomal Cav1.2 cleavage to barrier disruption. We show that the voltage-gated calcium channel Cav1.2 is aberrantly upregulated in the intestinal epithelium of UC patients and murine colitis models. Upon OMV internalization, increased caspase-5 is recruited to early endosomes, where it promotes the generation of the Cav1.2 C-terminal fragment (CCt), thereby facilitating LPS release from OMVs into the cytosol. Mechanistically, caspase-5 is required for and co-translocates with CCt into the nucleus, where they co-bind to the proximal CDH1 promoter region, repressing E-cadherin transcription and impairing barrier integrity. Furthermore, by rationally designing, we identify a small molecule DC-SG003 that enhances the interaction between the upstream orchestrator SNX10 and the E3 ubiquitin ligase MYCBP2. This promotes the ubiquitination-mediated degradation of SNX10, thereby providing a compelling pharmacological strategy to dismantle this cascade and restore epithelial barrier function.

articles.title: Oxidative DNA damage in workers from anatomic pathology laboratories exposed to low formaldehyde concentrations.
articles.abstract: Formaldehyde (FA) is widely used in pathological anatomy laboratories, where healthcare workers may experience occupational exposure. This multicenter study integrated environmental monitoring and biological effect biomarkers to assess FA exposure and early cyto-genotoxic, oxidative, and inflammatory responses in 85 workers potentially exposed to FA from an established Italian Network of six hospitals and in a control group of 99 non-exposed subjects. Airborne FA concentrations were measured using active or passive sampling strategies, while exposed workers and controls were investigated through the buccal micronucleus cytome (BMCyt) assay, the Fpg-modified comet assay, serum cytokine analysis by ELISA, and a self-reported health questionnaire. Environmental monitoring showed marked variability across hospitals and work areas, with most concentrations below occupational exposure limits. Biomonitoring revealed increased oxidative DNA damage in exposed workers as indicated by Fpg-comet. Selected BMCyt alterations, such as decreases in binucleated and karyolitic cells, suggested possible effects on epithelial cell cycle. In contrast, direct DNA damage, buccal micronucleus frequency, and circulating TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8 levels did not show consistent exposure-related increases. Questionnaire data indicated a higher occurrence of some self-reported skin and respiratory outcomes among exposed workers, although these findings remain to be explored further. These findings support oxidative DNA damage as one of the earliest detectable biological responses to occupational formaldehyde exposure, even under exposure conditions generally compliant with current occupational limits.

articles.title: Pharmacological characterization of emerging hexahydrocannabinol-derived semi-synthetic cannabinoids at the cannabinoid type 1 receptor using a β-arrestin2 recruitment assay.
articles.abstract: Semi-synthetic cannabinoids (SSCs) represent a rapidly expanding subclass of cannabinoids on the recreational drug market. Among these, structurally modified hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) derivatives have become particularly prominent. Fourteen HHC-derived SSCs were investigated, comprising C3 butyl to nonyl (C4-C9) side chain variants and C1-esterified derivatives of HHC and hexahydrocannabiphorol (HHCP). For each compound, the individual 9(R)- and 9(S)-epimers were evaluated. As a proxy for abuse potential, the compounds (picomolar-micromolar concentrations) were evaluated for cannabinoid type 1 receptor (CB1) activation potential using a cell-based β-arrestin2 recruitment bioassay, enabling determination of potency (EC50) and efficacy (Emax) values. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis demonstrated that elongation of the C3 alkyl side chain increased efficacy (C4 < C5 < C6 < C8 < C9) while generally reducing potency (C4 ≥ C5 ≈ C6 ≥ C8 > C9). The heptyl derivatives represented an exception to this trend, showing comparable or reduced efficacy relative to their hexyl counterparts, while maintaining similar or slightly increased potency. Notably, the C8 and C9 derivatives displayed markedly high efficacies, approaching or even exceeding the efficacy of the synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonist reference CP55,940. C1 esterification markedly reduced potency, with a less pronounced effect on efficacy. Across all compounds, the 9(R)-epimers were consistently more potent than their 9(S)-counterparts, while effects on efficacy were more variable and dependent on the specific structural modification. Overall, these findings enabled differentiation between compounds with negligible, comparable or higher activity at CB1 than ∆9-THC. This information may support healthcare workers and allow prioritization of substances that warrant extra surveillance.

articles.title: Hazard characterization of Alternaria toxins: filling data gaps on in vitro genotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Alternaria toxins are naturally occurring food contaminants with limited and often inconsistent genotoxicity and mutagenicity data. Within the European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC), an OECD-aligned in vitro testing strategy was applied to fill existing data gaps and to characterize the genotoxic potential of major Alternaria toxins using high-purity test materials. Mutagenicity was assessed using bacterial reverse mutation test (OECD TG 471) and SOS/umu assay, while chromosomal damage was assessed using the in vitro micronucleus (MN) assay (OECD TG 487) in TK6 and HepG2 cells, complemented by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and γH2AX assay in HepaRG cells. Alternariol (AOH), alternariol monomethyl ether (AME), and altertoxin-I (ATX-I) showed clear mutagenicity in bacteria, whereas altenuene (ALT), tenuazonic acid (TeA), and tentoxin (TEN) were negative under the tested conditions. In mammalian cells, AOH, AME, and ATX-I induced MN formation in TK6 cells at concentrations ≥ 5.5 µM, ≥ 2.5 µM, and ≥ 0.21 µM, respectively, with FISH analysis supporting a clastogenic mode of action. In HepG2 cells, all tested toxins induced chromosomal damage, with effect threshold ranging from ≥ 6.25 µM (AOH) to ≥ 50 µM (TeA). γH2AX induction confirmed DNA damage for AOH and ATX-I, and at higher concentrations for TeA (1000 µM). Overall, the data indicate clear in vitro genotoxic potential for AOH, AME, and ATX-I and provide evidence of chromosomal damage for ALT, TEN, and TeA, thereby reducing critical data gaps for hazard assessment.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of adjuvant glucocorticoid therapy for Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) in patients positive for HIV: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of glucocorticoids as adjuvant therapy for Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) in patients positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). METHODS: Clinical randomized controlled trials or clinical controlled trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of glucocorticoids as adjuvant therapy for PCP in patients who are HIV-positive were retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Data extraction and methodological quality assessment were performed for eligible studies. Meta-analysis and systematic evaluation were conducted using RevMan v.5.1 and STATA v.12.0 software. RESULTS: Nine articles (13 studies) were included. Compared with the controls, patients treated with glucocorticoids had significantly lower mortality rates (OR = 0.41, 95% CI [0.28-0.59], P < 0.00001), early deterioration rates (OR = 0.08, 95% CI [0.02-0.39], P = 0.002), and lower mechanical ventilation rates (OR = 0.32, 95% CI [0.19-0.55], P < 0.0001). Regarding safety, the incidence of adverse effects did not differ significantly between the two groups (OR = 0.74, 95% CI [0.33-1.70], P = 0.48). CONCLUSION: Adjuvant glucocorticoid therapy significantly reduces mortality, early deterioration, and mechanical ventilation rates in patients who are HIV-positive with PCP without increasing adverse reactions. Glucocorticoids may serve as a viable adjuvant treatment option for PCP in patients who are HIV-positive. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/home, identifier CRD420261418795.

articles.title: Polydeoxyribonucleotide and polynucleotide effects in musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The rising prevalence of degenerative musculoskeletal disorders and sports injuries has generated interest in regenerative medicine. Polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN) and polynucleotide (PN), extracted from salmonid (Salmonidae) germ-cell DNA, are biomacromolecules with extracellular matrix regenerative, pro-angiogenic, and anti-inflammatory properties. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically analyze the clinical and preclinical research trends in PDRN and PN injection therapy in the musculoskeletal field. EVIDENCE REVIEW: Studies on PDRN and PN injection therapy published before March 2026 were retrieved from 10 databases (4 English-, 1 Chinese-, 1 Japanese-, and 4 Korean-language). Clinical studies comprised randomized controlled and clinical studies of adults with musculoskeletal and associated neurological pain; preclinical studies comprised experimental studies using musculoskeletal and related neurological pain models. FINDINGS: Of the 13,267 records retrieved, 38 (28 clinical and 10 preclinical studies) were included. The clinical studies reported disorders of the knee, shoulder, temporomandibular joint, wrist, ankle/foot, elbow, and spine, reporting overall improvements in pain (visual analog and numerical rating scales) and function (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index and maximum mouth opening); however, between-group significance varied by disease site and design, particularly with hyaluronic acid comparators. Preclinically, an adenosine A2A receptor-cAMP-PKA-CREB pathway has been proposed, with suppression of M1 and activation of M2 macrophages and upregulation of vascular endothelial growth factor, fibroblast growth factor, and transforming growth factor-β1, promoting type I collagen formation and tendon-to-bone junction reinforcement, while exerting anti-apoptotic effects via caspase-3/9 inhibition. These actions translated into biomechanical outcomes, such as load-to-failure and locomotor recovery. No serious adverse events attributable to PDRN or PN were reported in the available clinical studies; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously, as adverse event assessment and reporting were incomplete and inconsistent across studies. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Available evidence suggests potential improvements in pain and function following PDRN/PN treatment; however, the certainty of the evidence remains limited because of methodological limitations, heterogeneous study designs, and inconsistent comparative effects. The limited quality and geographic representativeness of the evidence warrant rigorous, prospectively registered, large-scale, multinational randomized controlled trials. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261363033, identifier CRD420261363033 and https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261363211, identifier CRD420261363211.

articles.title: Clinical research landscape and evidence gaps in Traditional Chinese Medicine for recurrent urinary tract infections: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To map the clinical research landscape of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for the prevention and treatment of recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs), identify major gaps in study design and reporting, and inform the design of future clinical research. METHODS: We conducted a scoping review in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). On 1 May 2026, we searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database. The search covered records from database inception through 30 April 2026. Eligible reports were primary clinical studies evaluating botanical-drug preparations or other TCM-related interventions for rUTIs. We descriptively summarized study design, diagnostic criteria, interventions, outcome measures, follow-up, safety reporting, and selected methodological reporting features. For botanical interventions, we additionally mapped taxonomic identifiability and the reporting of composition, preparation or extraction, source or manufacturer, batch, and chemical characterization. The protocol was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/BYNFM). RESULTS: We included 91 clinical studies published between 1996 and 2026, comprising 74 randomized controlled trials (81.3%), eight non-randomized controlled trials (8.8%), seven case series (7.7%), and two retrospective studies (2.2%). Eighty-seven studies were conducted in mainland China, with one study each conducted in the United Kingdom, Iran, Ukraine, and Germany. Eighteen different terms were used to describe rUTIs. Twenty-eight studies (30.8%) did not report explicit diagnostic criteria, and 11 (12.1%) included mixed populations with upper and lower urinary tract infections. Botanical-drug decoctions were the most common intervention form, occurring in 72 studies (79.1%), and treatment duration ranged from 1 to 24 weeks. Among the 89 studies involving botanical interventions, 73 contained at least one medicinal-drug term that could not be linked unambiguously to a single species, 10 provided insufficient compositional information for taxonomic assessment, and the reported components were taxonomically resolved in six studies. Recurrence-related outcomes were reported in 48 studies (52.7%), whereas safety information was not reported in 60 studies (65.9%). Blinding was reported in eight studies (8.8%), and ethical approval was reported in 23 (25.3%). TCM syndrome differentiation was reported in 38 studies (41.8%), with considerable variation in the diagnostic standards used. CONCLUSION: Clinical research on TCM for rUTIs has expanded, but cumulative evidence development remains constrained by interconnected inconsistencies in population definition, intervention characterization, recurrence and safety assessment, and methodological reporting. More complete methodological reporting co-occurred with broader and more clinically informative outcome assessment, suggesting that reporting standards and outcome-set development should be advanced together. Standardized rUTI definitions, a core outcome set centred on recurrence and safety, and integration of reproducible TCM syndrome criteria with clinically relevant biomedical phenotypes are priorities for building a more interpretable and internationally comparable evidence base. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/BYNFM, identifier 10.17605/OSF.IO/BYNFM.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in diabetic kidney disease: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: AIMS: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRAs) in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched four databases to 31 July 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nsMRAs with placebo in adults with DKD. Pooled estimates used random-effects models, with mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes, each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2, and certainty of evidence with GRADE. RESULTS: Eight RCTs (15,143 patients) were included. nsMRAs reduced log-transformed UACR (MD -0.36 log mg/g, 95% CI -0.44 to -0.28; n = 14,512 from 8 trials, predominantly driven by finerenone (5 of 8 trials), with significant drug-type interaction; P < 0.00001) and systolic BP (MD -4.72 mmHg, 95% CI -8.64 to -0.80; n = 7,538 from 3 trials (6 trials reported systolic BP; only 3 were poolable); predominantly driven by FIGARO-DKD; P = 0.02), but increased serum potassium (MD 0.22 mmol/L, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.29; n = 1,468 from 4 trials (6 trials reported serum potassium; FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD excluded); P < 0.00001) and induced early eGFR decline (MD -3.01 mL/min/1.73 m2, 95% CI -4.46 to -1.56; n = 1,218 from 3 trials; P < 0.0001). Hyperkalemia risk was higher (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.99 to 2.52; n = 14,734 from 6 trials; P < 0.00001), whereas overall adverse events, eGFR decline, and acute kidney injury did not differ. GRADE certainty was low for UACR, systolic BP, serum potassium, and early eGFR decline, and moderate for hyperkalemia. CONCLUSION: In DKD, nsMRAs may reduce UACR and systolic BP. However, UACR was driven by finerenone with significant drug-type interaction, requiring agent-specific interpretation. Systolic BP was driven by FIGARO-DKD. Furthermore, nsMRAs may increase serum potassium and hyperkalemia risk, although the serum potassium analysis excluded two large trials. nsMRAs may also cause early hemodynamic eGFR decline. Notably, this review assessed only surrogate endpoints and safety outcomes. Several outcomes were supported by only 3-4 trials. Given these limitations and low-to-moderate certainty, findings warrant cautious interpretation and risk-benefit assessment. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251072300, identifier CRD420251072300.

articles.title: A Precise Activity System for Pharmacogenetics Based on Estimation of CYP2D6 Allelic Percentage Activity from the International CEPAM Database.
articles.abstract: The polymorphic enzyme CYP2D6 contributes to the metabolism of many frequently prescribed drugs, causing substantial variability in drug exposure and treatment outcomes. Genotype-based dosing recommendations currently rely on drug-agnostic categorical CYP2D6 allele activity values (AVs), potentially leading to imprecise CYP2D6 phenotype classification and under-/overdosing of numerous medications. To further advance precision dosing, we developed a CYP2D6 percentage activity (CYP2D6-PA) framework by estimating CYP2D6 allelic percentage activity (CYP2D6-APA) from 0% (no activity) to 100% (CYP2D6*1-normalized reference activity) using tamoxifen and its active metabolite Z-endoxifen as a model substrate. By leveraging nonlinear mixed-effects modeling of the international CEPAM database (>7,000 patients from 31 studies), bias-corrected CYP2D6-APAs were estimated, considering global allele distributions, additional covariates, and limited CYP2D6 genotyping. Estimated CYP2D6-APAs spanned 0%-100%, several deviating substantially from their categorical AVs. In particular, CYP2D6*2 and *35 (normal function, AV = 1), and *17 and *29 (decreased function, AV = 0.5) showed lower CYP2D6-APAs of 64-68% and 29%, respectively. Conversely, CYP2D6*9 (decreased function, AV = 0.25) showed a higher CYP2D6-APA (52%). Each additional allele copy exhibited 68% of the activity of the first copy, less than the twofold increase assumed by AVs. Neglecting limited genotyping (alleles misclassified as reference CYP2D6*1), caused CYP2D6-APA overestimation by 1.1-fold. Using CYP2D6-APAs instead of AVs translated to changes in predicted individual Z-endoxifen concentrations (-22.3% to 40.0%). While substrate specificity of empirically derived robust tamoxifen CYP2D6-APAs requires evaluation, CYP2D6-PA provides a framework applicable to other substrates/pharmacogenes. Thus, CYP2D6-PA lays the foundation for revising genotype-to-phenotype translation systems, improving precision of pharmacogenetics-guided dosing and optimizing treatment outcomes upon prospective validation.

articles.title: First factor XIa inhibitor nabs FDA approval for stroke prevention.
Effects of scheduled ibuprofen combined with diclofenac suppository on postoperative pain in children undergoing pectus excavatum correction: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are widely used for postoperative acute pain management. However, the safety and efficacy of postoperative scheduled oral ibuprofen remain unclear in children. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of scheduled ibuprofen combined with diclofenac suppository for postoperative analgesia in children following the Nuss procedure for pectus excavatum. METHODS: Sixty patients who underwent the Nuss procedure from September 2024 to August 2025 were randomly divided and assigned to either the experimental or control group. The experimental group received scheduled ibuprofen combined with a diclofenac suppository, whereas the control group received a diclofenac suppository and ibuprofen on demand. The postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) scores, supplemental opioid consumption, time to first ambulation, length of hospital stay, and incidence of adverse events were recorded for both groups. RESULTS: The VAS scores at 6-24 h postoperatively were significantly lower for the experimental group than the control group (p < 0.05). The experimental group required less opioids than the control group (62.4 ± 5.7 vs. 67.5 ± 6.4 µg, p = 0.002; difference: -5.167 µg, 95% confidence interval: -8.325 to -2.008). Additionally, the time to first ambulation (5.9 ± 0.6 vs. 6.4 ± 0.7 h, p = 0.005; difference: -0.486 h, 95% confidence interval: -0.924 to -0.076) and length of hospital stay (6.8 ± 0.8 vs. 7.3 ± 0.8 days, p = 0.022; difference: -0.500 days, 95% confidence interval: -0.924 to -0.076) were shorter for the experimental group than the control group. The incidence of adverse events was similar for both groups (p > 0.05). CONCLUSION: This study indicates that scheduled ibuprofen combined with diclofenac suppository provides effective analgesia following the Nuss procedure, reduces opioid consumption, and promotes recovery. No serious NSAID-related adverse events were observed during the short postoperative observation period. However, the study was not powered to establish safety or exclude clinically important differences in uncommon adverse events. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2400089927.

articles.title: Threshold-triggered microneedle applicators: converting user-applied force into reproducible dissolving microneedle insertion for global vaccination.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaccine distribution in low- and middle-income countries is constrained by healthcare workforce shortages - averaging one health worker per 435 people - and by unreliable facility infrastructure. Dissolving microneedle patches address these bottlenecks by reducing cold-chain reliance and enabling dose-sparing immunization through skin-resident antigen-presenting cells. However, reproducible administration by minimally trained personnel remains a critical barrier to deployment. AREA COVERED: This review examines five representative applicator architectures from the peer-reviewed and patent literature, detailing how each converts variable user input into a standardized, high-velocity impact that overcomes rate-dependent skin viscoelasticity to ensure deep, reproducible stratum corneum penetration. Each is evaluated against three prerequisites for global deployment: sufficient insertion force and rate, low-cost manufacturability, and power independence. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Patents were searched from 2004 to June 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Validation remains weighted toward mechanical and ex vivo testing, so the field's engineering maturity runs ahead of its translational readiness. Realizing the public health potential of microneedle vaccines will require user-independent operation, scalable manufacturing, and integration of threshold-triggered mechanisms with patch design so that delivered dose and immune response are reproducible. Eliminating pre-loaded energy components is central to the cost competitiveness that mass immunization in resource-limited settings demands.

articles.title: Targeting neddylation in cancer: molecular mechanisms, translational advances, and therapeutic challenges.
articles.abstract: Neddylation is a ubiquitin-like post-translational modification that regulates cullin-RING ligases and selected non-cullin substrates involved in cell-cycle progression, DNA replication licensing, DNA-damage repair, apoptosis, hypoxic signaling, inflammatory responses, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metabolic adaptation, and immune regulation. Many tumors rely on aberrant neddylation-dependent protein turnover to sustain proliferation, survival, metastatic plasticity, and therapeutic resistance, making this pathway a compelling anticancer target. This review outlines the molecular architecture of the NEDD8 cascade, encompassing NEDD8 activation, E2-mediated conjugation, E3/co-E3-facilitated ligation, deneddylation, and the central role of cullin-RING ligases as oncogenic effectors. It also examines the principal classes of neddylation-pathway inhibitors, including the first-in-class NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN4924, newer NAE inhibitors such as TAS4464, emerging UBE2M- and UBE2F-directed approaches, DCN1/DCUN1-targeted inhibitors, and natural product-derived or other experimental compounds. Preclinical evidence across hematologic malignancies, gastrointestinal and genitourinary cancers, thoracic and head-and-neck tumors, brain tumors, and pediatric cancers indicates that neddylation inhibition can suppress tumor growth and enhance responses to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, apoptosis-targeted agents, proteasome inhibition, autophagy modulation, and immunotherapy. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains constrained by inadequate patient selection, context-dependent substrate accumulation, adaptive resistance, complex immune effects, and limited therapeutic windows. Future development should therefore move beyond empirical pan-pathway inhibition toward biomarker-guided, tumor-context-specific precision strategies integrating selective E1, E2, and E3 inhibitors, rational combination regimens, pharmacodynamic monitoring, resistance profiling, immune-state assessment, and tumor-targeted delivery systems.

articles.title: Recent advances in the pharmacological effects and mechanisms of borneol and borneol-containing formulations in central nervous system diseases.
articles.abstract: Borneol is an aromatic medicinal agent widely used in traditional Chinese medicine, both as a standalone component and as an ingredient in multi-herb formulations. Its pharmacological relevance to central nervous system (CNS) disorders has attracted increasing attention, particularly in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, ischemic stroke, and glioma. Accumulating evidence indicates that borneol may influence multiple pathophysiological processes, including brain-barrier function and drug delivery, neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, neurotransmitter homeostasis and neuronal excitability, cellular injury and death, and the clearance of pathological substances and post-injury repair. Here, we integrate and compare these mechanisms across disease contexts. Notably, although several actions of borneol appear to converge across CNS disorders, others are strongly disease- and context-dependent; for example, its effects on brain-barrier permeability, oxidative stress, and cell death may differ in direction according to disease pathology and therapeutic intent. Pharmacokinetic studies support measurable brain exposure to borneol, yet direct comparative evidence of pharmacological activity, brain disposition, and human pharmacokinetics among borneol preparations of different botanical origins and stereochemical configurations remains scarce. Borneol-containing formulations also exhibit multi-level pharmacological effects; however, because most studies lack borneol-alone, borneol-depleted, or add-back controls, these effects cannot be unequivocally attributed to borneol itself. Overall, the current evidence base remains dominated by cellular and animal studies, with several proposed mechanisms inferred primarily from changes in molecular expression or computational predictions. Robust causal validation, high-quality clinical evidence, and long-term safety data are still limited. Future studies should therefore define the dose-exposure-response relationships and disease-specific therapeutic windows of different borneol preparations, establish the independent contribution of borneol within complex formulations, and determine its genuine therapeutic value and long-term safety through rigorous mechanistic and clinical investigation.

articles.title: Endolysins for precision antimicrobial therapy and rapid bacterial detection: translational challenges and future directions.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of alternative therapeutic and diagnostic strategies. Among emerging approaches, bacteriophage-derived endolysins have attracted considerable attention as promising tools for combating bacterial infections. Endolysins are phage-encoded peptidoglycan-degrading enzymes that have shown significant potential for both antimicrobial and diagnostic applications against a wide range of bacterial pathogens. This review summarizes the current knowledge of endolysins, highlighting their rapid bacteriolytic activity, high target specificity, and diverse therapeutic and diagnostic applications. Beyond their antimicrobial potential, endolysin-derived cell wall-binding domains (CBDs) and phage receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) have emerged as highly specific recognition molecules for the rapid detection of bacterial pathogens in clinical diagnostics and food safety. Rapid and accurate pathogen detection is essential for timely disease management, infection control, and the prevention of foodborne contamination. Despite these promising attributes, several challenges continue to limit the clinical and industrial translation of endolysins, including constraints related to protein expression, stability, formulation, and large-scale production. Furthermore, the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria remains a major obstacle to endolysin activity by restricting access to the peptidoglycan layer. Recent advances in protein engineering, membrane-permeabilization strategies, and delivery approaches have provided promising solutions to overcome these limitations. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive overview of the current advances, translational challenges, and future prospects of engineered endolysins as precision antimicrobial agents and diagnostic tools for combating antimicrobial-resistant bacterial pathogens.

articles.title: Advanced Thinking and Reasoning Paradigms in the Architecture of Preclinical and Clinical Pharmacology Research.
articles.abstract: To conduct scientific research, researchers need methodological expertise and a range of cognitive skills. Nevertheless, researchers treat these cognitive processes implicitly and do not regard them as an explicit element of research methodology. This article examines the structure of scientific inquiry, focusing on thinking: creative, divergent, lateral, vertical, convergent, critical, Janusian, and reasoning: abductive, deductive, inductive. It examines how these processes identify knowledge gaps, formulate research questions and hypotheses, select study designs, and interpret evidence. Instead of viewing thinking and reasoning as sequential stages, we propose an integrated, iterative approach in which these processes interact at all stages of the research cycle. This framework addresses the cognitive gap between conceptualizing a research problem and conducting a study. It also stresses that methodological accuracy, reproducibility, and dependability depend on the quality of the cognitive decisions that accompany experimental and clinical investigation. Since artificial intelligence is widely used to speed up literature analysis, hypothesis generation, data analysis, and experimental design, human judgment is still needed to assess the significance of the questions, the plausibility of the explanations, the validity of the study designs, and the adequacy of the evidence. This article provides a unified conceptual structure for incorporating thinking and reasoning processes in preclinical and clinical research.

articles.title: Epigenetic Allostasis in Alcohol Use Disorder: A Metabolic-Chromatin Framework Linking DNA Methylation, Circuit Remodeling, and Precision Therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a chronic relapsing disorder characterized by persistent dysregulation of reward, stress, and executive circuits. Although acute ethanol effects on neurotransmission are well established, the molecular mechanisms that stabilize long-term vulnerability remain unclear. Building on established allostatic and epigenetic-allostatic models, we develop an expanded framework in which repeated alcohol exposure can drive a transition from adaptive, transient chromatin remodeling toward more persistent epigenetic states across key neural circuits. We integrate evidence from histone modifications, DNA methylation, and metabolic regulation, highlighting how alcohol-induced oxidative stress and disruption of one-carbon metabolism lead to S-adenosylmethionine depletion and methylation instability. These processes converge to form a metabolic-epigenetic trap, reinforcing transcriptional repression of plasticity-related genes. We synthesize circuit-specific changes in the amygdala, prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, and hippocampus, and incorporate emerging human postmortem and single-nucleus multiomic data that support cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling. In addition, we examine neuroimmune-epigenetic interactions and developmental and sex-dependent exposures as amplifiers of epigenetic vulnerability. Finally, we evaluate therapeutic strategies ranging from selective histone deacetylase inhibition to locus-specific epigenome editing, emphasizing the critical importance of treatment timing and circuit specificity. Together, this expanded framework conceptualizes AUD as a disorder in which maladaptive genomic stability may contribute to persistent circuit dysfunction and identifies epigenetic-metabolic coupling as a testable target for next-generation therapeutics.

articles.title: NAT10-mediated ac4C RNA modification in disease: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C) is a conserved RNA modification associated with RNA stability, translation and cellular adaptation. N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) modifies several RNA classes and also has functions that can be separated from RNA acetylation. Consequently, NAT10-dependent phenotypes do not by themselves establish a causal role for ac4C on a particular transcript. This review connects NAT10 structure and substrate recruitment with detection methods, disease mechanisms and therapeutic development. We distinguish site-resolved ac4C causality, transcript-associated acetylation with RNA-fate evidence, NAT10-dependent effects with unverified ac4C involvement, and pharmacological effects with unresolved target attribution. Evidence is traced from the modification event through RNA fate, pathway output and cellular-state maintenance to disease phenotype. Representative mechanisms are assessed individually, including separate genetic and drug-derived conclusions. We consider ac4C as a potential context-dependent post-transcriptional state stabilizer, rather than a universally activating or irreversible mark. Protective functions in germ cells and selected inflammatory responses constrain extrapolation from cancer. We critically assess Remodelin and emerging NAT10-directed compounds, distinguish catalytic inhibition from protein depletion, and discuss the assays, exposure measurements and pharmacodynamic markers needed for translation. Selective RNA acetylation inhibition and clinically validated ac4C biomarkers remain development objectives.

articles.title: Sleep and circadian disruption as systemic drivers of breast cancer metastasis: A tri-pathway mechanistic model.
articles.abstract: Sleep deficiency and circadian disruption are emerging modifiable risk factors in breast cancer. However, their specific role in driving metastasis remains incompletely defined. This review maps circadian disturbance to metastatic competence through three convergent systemic pathways. First is neuroendocrine disruption via melatonin suppression. Second is immunological dysregulation characterized by chronic inflammation and myeloid derived suppressor cell expansion. Third is metabolic reprogramming involving insulin resistance and altered adipokine signaling. These converging signals lower critical barriers at every step of metastasis. They promote epithelial mesenchymal transition and local invasion. They support circulating tumor cell survival. They enable pre metastatic niche formation. They also trigger reactivation of dormant micrometastases. We evaluate clinical biomarkers of circadian disruption including cortisol rhythms, urinary melatonin, and actigraphy. We link these sleep metrics to patient outcomes. We also discuss therapeutic opportunities such as melatonin supplementation, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, and personalized chrono chemotherapy. By establishing circadian health as an actionable axis in metastasis prevention, this review provides a framework for integrating chronobiology into breast cancer management and survivorship care.

articles.title: Regional cardiac ectopic fat: From pathophysiology to therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, while its pathogenesis is complex and has not been fully elucidated. Cardiac ectopic fat deposition, primarily including epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT), and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT), is increasingly recognized for its role in cardiovascular dysfunction. In obesity and insulin resistance, these fat depots may undergo pathological expansion and functional remodelling. This pathological transition involves inflammatory activation, lipotoxicity, oxidative stress, fibrotic remodelling, and metabolic dysfunction, contributing to cardiovascular injury through distinct pathways. EAT is closely linked to myocardial and atrial remodelling, whereas PVAT contributes to vascular inflammation and dysfunction. PAT is more closely associated with systemic adiposity and cardiometabolic risk. With the increasing prevalence of obesity and metabolic syndrome, the clinical burden associated with cardiac ectopic fat is expected to increase. This review summarizes the anatomical localization, physiological functions, obesity-associated remodelling and pathogenic mechanisms of ectopic fat in distinct cardiac regions, along with potential intervention strategies. Lifestyle modification, pharmacological treatment, and bariatric surgery may modulate regional fat accumulation and function. Understanding the distinct characteristics of these depots may support improved cardiovascular risk assessment and more targeted therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: Microneedle-based delivery strategies for cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Microneedle (MN) technologies are currently investigated as versatile delivery platforms for cancer immunotherapy. They offer minimally invasive and localized delivery, and may enable sustained release while overcoming several limitations of conventional systemic administration. In this review, we discuss the relation between MN design and the delivery of different cancer immunotherapies, with a particular focus on matching MN technologies to different therapeutic strategies. We first describe the main MN approaches, including dissolving, direct-injection, melting, and diffusion-based systems, and their applications in cancer immunotherapy. We then categorize these applications into four major strategies: cancer vaccination including both prophylactic and therapeutic vaccines, induction of immunogenic cell death using chemotherapeutics and photosensitizers, systemic immunotherapy through transdermal delivery, and local immunomodulation through intratumoral delivery of immunotherapeutic agents. Finally, we discuss current challenges and perspectives for translating MN-based cancer immunotherapies toward clinical application, including formulation flexibility, manufacturing scalability, dose control, and regulatory considerations.

articles.title: The Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) paradox in cancer: From tumor microenvironment remodeling to therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), encoded by the SERPINE1 gene, is a key regulator of the fibrinolytic system through inhibition of the plasminogen activators urokinase (uPA) and tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA). Although this canonical function would be expected to limit extracellular matrix degradation and tumor invasion, elevated PAI-1 expression is consistently associated with tumor progression and poor clinical outcomes across multiple cancer types. This apparent contradiction, known as the "PAI-1 paradox," highlights the diverse biological functions of PAI-1 beyond fibrinolysis. Within the tumor microenvironment, PAI-1 regulates several hallmarks of cancer through interactions with extracellular matrix components and receptors such as LRP1, uPAR, and integrins. These interactions influence angiogenesis, apoptosis resistance, tumor cell migration, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Emerging evidence also indicates that PAI-1 shapes the immune microenvironment by modulating immune cell recruitment and macrophage polarization, although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Clinically, SERPINE1 overexpression correlates with poor prognosis in numerous malignancies, including colorectal, lung, breast, and gastric cancers. Pharmacological targeting of the PAI-1 axis with small-molecule inhibitors or neutralizing antibodies shows antitumor activity in preclinical models, and the oral inhibitor TM5614 has reached phase III clinical trial in chronic myeloid leukemia and melanoma. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge of PAI-1 regulation and function in cancer and discusses therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway.

articles.title: Understanding pharmacokinetics of novel prolonged release dienogest 2 mg / ethinyl-estradiol 0.02 mg oral contraceptive formulation: clinical applications.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) have traditionally evolved through changes in estrogen and progestin type and dose to improve safety and tolerability. More recently, drug-delivery technology has emerged as an additional strategy to modify pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles without altering hormonal components. AREAS COVERED: A structured search of MEDLINE and regulatory sources was conducted to review the PK and pharmacodynamic characteristics of a prolonged-release COC containing dienogest (DNG) 2 mg and ethinylestradiol (EE) 0.02 mg, and to explore their clinical implications. Compared with immediate-release formulations, prolonged-release DNG/EE produces delayed peak concentrations, lower plasma peak levels, and reduced intra-day hormonal fluctuations while maintaining comparable overall exposure. EXPERT OPINION: Clinical evidence indicates contraceptive efficacy comparable to other COCs, with improved bleeding control compared with an immediate-release formulation. Both the intrinsic endometrial effects of DNG and more stable hormonal exposure may contribute to this finding. The formulation also provides antiandrogenic effects that may benefit hirsutism and acne. The safety profile appears broadly consistent with other low-dose COCs, although the effect on thromboembolic risk remains uncertain. Prolonged-release technology adds a new dimension to contraceptive choice and may facilitate individualized COC selection. Further comparative and post-marketing studies are needed to establish its clinical advantages and long-term safety.

articles.title: AI-enabled drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease: from computational nomination to pharmacological proof.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the scale and speed of drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Transcriptomic signature matching, network-based systems pharmacology, real-world data pharmacoepidemiology and multi-omics machine learning have generated hundreds of candidate drugs, while repurposed agents account for 35% (56 of 158) of drugs and 42% (15 of 36) of Phase 3 agents in the 2026 AD pipeline. Clinical translation, however, remains unproven. Randomised trials of GLP-1 receptor agonists illustrate the gap between prioritisation and therapeutic proof: semaglutide did not slow clinical progression in evoke and evoke+, while liraglutide did not improve the primary FDG-PET endpoint in ELAD. We examine four complementary evidence domains, defining what each can and cannot establish, and position large language models as a cross-cutting tool for evidence synthesis and knowledge-graph reasoning rather than an independent source of biological evidence. Rather than cataloguing methods and candidates, we appraise leading drugs at the individual-molecule level and propose explicit criteria for progression from computational nomination to clinical testing. The framework defines seven requirements for clinical progression: disease-stage matching, adequate site-of-action exposure, including CNS exposure for central mechanisms, mechanistic validation in human-relevant models, biomarker-stratified trial design, convergence across independent evidence domains, causal inference with explicit boundary conditions, and mechanism-aligned endpoints with predefined stopping rules. AI has improved candidate prioritisation in AD, but clinical value will depend on converting ranked hypotheses into pharmacologically plausible and prospectively testable programmes.

articles.title: Safety of long-term use of potassium-competitive acid blockers: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) reversibly inhibit gastric H+/K+-ATPase, providing rapid and potent acid suppression. They are increasingly used for gastroesophageal reflux disease, peptic ulcer disease, and Helicobacter pylori eradication. As maintenance therapy expands, long-term safety has drawn growing attention. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the available evidence on the long-term safety of P-CABs, distinguishing established findings from potential safety signals. METHODS: This narrative review drew on searches of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov through 30 June 2026. Studies with at least 24 weeks of treatment or follow-up formed the longer-term human evidence base. Evidence was synthesized by safety outcome, considering the specific agent and study design. CONCLUSION: Available comparative evidence, predominantly for vonoprazan, has not shown a substantially higher overall adverse event incidence than with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs). Sustained acid suppression can induce hypergastrinemia, which may be accompanied by parietal-cell hyperplasia, fundic gland dilatation, and other endoscopic mucosal changes. Evidence remains insufficient to determine the risks of rare or long-latency outcomes or to generalize long-term findings to all P-CABs. Long-term prescribing should include periodic reassessment of the indication and individualized monitoring.

articles.title: Omics-guided therapeutic translation in acute traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: Decades of trials evaluating secondary-injury targeted therapeutics in traumatic brain injury (TBI) have failed almost without exception, typically concluding that the intervention was ineffective. We argue that these failures stem largely from methodological limitations and should be reconceptualized. TBI pathobiology has traditionally been studied, stratified, and treated using single markers, isolated mechanisms, and discrete timepoints, despite being heterogeneous, compartmentalized, and temporally dynamic. High-dimensional omics, interpreted at the level of biological pathways rather than individual analytes, offers a direct means of addressing this complexity. Focusing on the acute phase of moderate-to-severe TBI, we define four recurrent failure modes in TBI therapeutic translation: the wrong patient, the wrong sample, the wrong window, and the wrong mechanism. For each, we identify targeted omics and pathway-level strategies that can mitigate these limitations and summarize what such approaches have revealed about TBI pathobiology. Finally, we argue that pathway-based predictive enrichment, combined with drug repurposing, is a promising near-term strategy that may improve the odds of detecting a real treatment effect where unselected trials have not.

articles.title: Targeting ferroptosis in rotenone-induced Parkinson's disease: from mechanistic insights to pharmacological interventions.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, leading to disabling motor and non-motor symptoms. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent oxidative cell death driven by lethal lipid peroxidation, has emerged in preclinical models as a candidate pathogenic mechanism in PD, although its causal centrality in human PD remains to be established. Rotenone, a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor widely used to model PD, recapitulates key clinical and pathological features of the disease. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that rotenone induces ferroptosis through a coordinated network of iron dyshomeostasis, inactivation of the System Xc--GPX4 antioxidant axis, dysregulated lipid metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, ferritinophagy-mediated iron release, neuroinflammation, and SIRT1-Nrf2 pathway suppression. Importantly, pharmacological targeting of these ferroptotic nodes-with agents such as Fer-1, iron chelators, Nrf2 activators, and modulators of ferritinophagy-effectively attenuates rotenone-induced neurodegeneration and restores motor function in preclinical models. This review systematically dissects the molecular circuitry of ferroptosis in rotenone -based PD models and evaluates the therapeutic potential of ferroptosis inhibitors, aiming to inform the development of disease-modifying strategies for PD.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence for Traditional Chinese Medicine classic formula development: a technology readiness assessment using metabolic syndrome as a case study.
articles.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas, developed through millennia of clinical practice, represent a rich legacy of approximately 100,000 documented prescriptions (99,584 named formula entries in the second edition of the Dictionary of Traditional Chinese Medicine Formulas), yet on average fewer than ten new TCM products were approved annually by China's NMPA from 2013 to 2024 (77 approvals in total). The experience-based screening paradigm is misaligned with the precision medicine framework demanded by metabolic syndrome (MetS), a multi-target disorder affecting an estimated 1.54 billion adults (95% CrI 1.35-1.76) in 2023. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-encompassing knowledge graphs (KGs), large language models (LLMs), and high-throughput experimentation-has been proposed as a solution, its actual readiness for TCM development remains unclear. This review critically examines KG, LLM, and high-throughput validation technologies enabling precision phytomedicine for MetS, providing a realistic roadmap for AI-driven TCM research and development. The three technology streams exhibit asymmetric readiness. At the stream level, knowledge-graph approaches span Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3-6, large language model approaches span TRL 1-5, and high-throughput validation platforms span TRL 3-5. LLM development is limited by three TCM-specific hallucination types that lack evaluation benchmarks. KG entity recognition is the most mature component, yet reasoning is hindered by the absence of negative data, missing dose-time dimensions, and unencoded monarch-minister-assistant-envoy hierarchies. High-throughput platforms are technically feasible but remain mismatched to MetS functional endpoints-tumor-derived organoid paradigms show limited direct transferability and would require substantial adaptation. Precision phytomedicine must follow a "foundations before algorithms" sequence: institutionalize negative data, build TCM-Hallu benchmarks, establish functional-endpoint evaluation, and develop AI-assisted regulatory review. Algorithmic advances will remain in an incomplete information space until knowledge infrastructure gaps are closed.

articles.title: Advances in platinum-based drug development for cervical cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a predominant malignancy of the female reproductive system and a critical global health challenge. Traditional platinum-based agents such as cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin, are cornerstones in postoperative adjuvant therapy, management of locally advanced cases, and systemic treatment of recurrent/metastatic disease. However, their clinical efficacy is frequently hampered by severe systemic toxicities and the emergence of chemoresistance. To address these bottlenecks, diverse nano-delivery platforms have been engineered to enhance bioavailability and mitigate adverse effects. This review systematically delineates the evolution of first-to third-generation platinum drugs, elucidating their molecular mechanisms of action specifically within the landscape of cervical cancer. Furthermore, we critically evaluate the clinical application of these agents and provide a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in nano-delivery systems, including targeted and stimuli-responsive carriers. By bridging traditional pharmacology with cutting-edge nanotechnology, this review offers strategic insights into achieving precise delivery and controlled release, potentially defining new paradigms for the next-generation of cervical cancer therapeutics.

articles.title: Context-dependent pharmacological effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in breast cancer from molecular mechanisms to clinical safety.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have become cornerstone therapeutics for type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, but their impact on breast cancer remains uncertain. Preclinical studies show context-dependent effects of GLP-1 RAs on breast-cancer cells. Direct evidence from breast-cancer models supports a pro-proliferative NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4)/reactive oxygen species (ROS) /VEGF pathway under supra-pharmacological exposure, whereas PI3K/Akt-mediated pro-survival signaling and cAMP/PKA/CREB-driven proliferation remain inferred from non-breast systems and require direct confirmation. Under obesity- and insulin-resistant conditions, indirect antitumor effects may occur through improved insulin sensitivity, altered adipokines, and remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials do not show a significant increase in breast-cancer risk (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.76-1.26), while some large observational cohorts report small risk differences that are susceptible to confounding and detection bias. Evidence for inter-agent differences is observational and limited by the absence of head-to-head randomized oncological comparisons. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence across three dimensions, namely, molecular subtype, drug exposure, and host metabolic status, and distinguishes direct breast-cancer evidence from mechanistic extrapolation. We outline evidence-informed clinical considerations and research priorities rather than definitive recommendations.

articles.title: Natural flavonoids in peptic ulcer disease: preclinical evidence for gastroprotection versus healing of established ulcers.
articles.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is a global health concern with a lifetime prevalence of 5%-10%. Current therapies may be limited by adverse effects and the increasing prevalence of drug-resistant Helicobacter pylori strains, highlighting the need for safer complementary approaches. Natural flavonoids have emerged as candidate bioactive compounds with gastroprotective properties in preclinical models. This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA 2020, summarizes preclinical evidence published between 2020 and 2025 on the gastroprotective (preventive) and ulcer-healing effects of isolated and chemically characterized flavonoids. PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched, and eligible studies were restricted to in vitro and/or in vivo experimental investigations. Fourteen studies were included, and their risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE and ToxRTool tools. Gastric injury was induced mainly by ethanol, indomethacin, aspirin, or acetic acid in rats and mice, complemented by two gastric cell models. Seven of the 13 in vivo studies used preventive protocols, whereas only four evaluated the healing of established ulcers; the remaining studies used concurrent, post-injury, or mixed protocols. Quercetin (three studies), apigenin, and myricetin (two studies each) were the most frequently investigated, whereas luteolin, naringenin, acacetin, rhamnetin, fisetin, genistein, and malvidin were each evaluated in a single study. These compounds were associated with reduced mucosal damage and with changes in markers of oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and mucosal defense; potential anti-H. pylori mechanisms are discussed on the basis of previous reviews. Overall, the available evidence supports gastroprotective activity of natural flavonoids in preclinical models, whereas evidence for ulcer healing remains limited. Most studies were rated as having an unclear risk of bias, and differences in models, doses, treatment timing, and bioavailability limit direct comparison between compounds. These preclinical findings cannot be considered evidence of clinical efficacy, and pharmacokinetic, safety, and well-designed clinical studies are required before any therapeutic use in PUD can be considered.

articles.title: Epimedium koreanum Nakai attenuates glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by suppressing ferroptosis via the KEAP1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 axis: comparative pharmacodynamic evaluation of four epimedium species and proteomic and metabolomic analyses of epk.
articles.abstract: Objective: The pharmacodynamics and underlying mechanisms of Epimedium (Yingyanghuo), a traditional Chinese medicine, were investigated in the context of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) management, with particular emphasis on ferroptosis inhibition.Methods: A rat model of GIOP was developed through dexamethasone (DEX) administration. Animals received extracts of the four Epimedium species; Epimedium koreanum Nakai (Epk) was selected for subsequent investigation owing to its superior preliminary efficacy. Evaluations encompassed bone microstructure, osteoclast activity, serum biomarkers of bone metabolism, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation and iron accumulation indicators (4-HNE and Fe2+), and ferroptosis-associated proteins (KEAP1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway). Integration of proteomics and metabolomics facilitated the identification of key pathways, followed by experimental validation of ferroptosis modulation.Results: Epk treatment mitigated DEX-induced bone loss, improved bone microarchitecture, and suppressed osteoclast activity. Multi-omics approaches uncovered reversal of 368 proteins and 127 metabolites in GIOP rats following Epk administration, with enrichment observed in ferroptosis, glutathione metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation. Treatment with Epk further reduced the elevated femoral 4-HNE and Fe2+ levels in GIOP rats. Epk treatment elevated NRF2, HO-1, SLC7A11, and GPX4 and reduced KEAP1 and P53 in bone tissue, consistent with suppression of ferroptosis-related signaling.Conclusion: Epimedium, with Epk as the prominent representative, confers substantial protection against GIOP, with effects associated with modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway and suppression of ferroptosis-related markers in bone tissue, thereby providing a basis for further investigation of its clinical potential in GIOP management.

articles.title: Ambrisentan ameliorates methotrexate nephrotoxicity through modulation of RhoA/ROCK and PI3K/MDM2-associated signaling: network pharmacology-guided discovery and in vivo confirmation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Methotrexate (MTX) is a potent antineoplastic agent; however, its clinical application is frequently limited by nephrotoxicity, which may result in treatment interruption. Previous evidence indicates that MTX can promote endothelin-1 (ET-1)-associated renal injury. Therefore, this study investigated whether blocking ET-1 receptors with Ambrisentan (AMB) could alleviate MTX-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). METHODS: Network pharmacology analysis was performed to identify potential targets and pathways associated with AMB and MTX-induced AKI. For In-vivo validation, twenty-four rats were divided into four groups: control, AMB, MTX, and MTX+AMB. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Network pharmacology identified 102 overlapping targets between AMB and MTX-induced AKI, with 20 hub genes identified through protein-protein interaction network analysis, highlighting PPAR-γ as a key target. KEGG pathway enrichment revealed the involvement of RhoA/ROCK and PI3K-associated signaling pathways, in correlation with inflammatory and apoptotic markers. Experimentally, AMB co-treatment improved renal function parameters and histopathological alterations, restored oxidative balance, and attenuated MTX-induced inflammatory and apoptotic responses, including ICAM-1, NF-κB, RhoA/ROCK, Bax, Caspase-3 and p53. Furthermore, AMB restored the expression of PPAR-γ, PI3K, MDM2, and Bcl-2, suggesting the involvement of PI3K/MDM2-associated signaling alterations in AMB-mediated nephroprotection. In conclusion, AMB may mitigate MTX-induced nephrotoxicity through modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Further studies are required to evaluate its effects on MTX pharmacokinetics, renal elimination, antineoplastic efficacy, and therapeutic potential in established MTX-induced AKI.

articles.title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation versus sham stimulation and dexamethasone versus amisulpride for preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic gynecologic surgery: protocol for a randomized 2 × 2 factorial trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a common complication after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Although multimodal prophylaxis is recommended, clinical practice still relies largely on pharmacologic interventions. Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) at the P6 acupoint may have potential benefit for PONV prevention. However, its effectiveness when incorporated into pharmacologic prophylaxis, and whether its effect varies according to the antiemetic used, remain unclear. This trial aims to evaluate the effect of P6-TEAS on PONV prevention in patients receiving dexamethasone or amisulpride. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial will enroll 212 women undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive one of four treatment combinations: TEAS plus dexamethasone, TEAS plus amisulpride, sham stimulation plus dexamethasone, or sham stimulation plus amisulpride. TEAS or sham stimulation will be delivered at the P6 acupoint in two 1-h sessions, before surgery and at 24 h after surgery. The primary outcome will be the incidence of PONV within 48 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include PONV-related symptoms and severity, use of rescue antiemetics, opioid consumption, pain scores, recovery milestones, patient satisfaction, QoR-15 scores, and length of hospital stay. Safety outcomes will include adverse events related to TEAS or study drugs and perioperative hemodynamic events requiring treatment. DISCUSSION: This trial will evaluate P6-TEAS versus sham stimulation as the primary comparison and provide exploratory estimates for the dexamethasone-versus-amisulpride comparison and the TEAS-by-drug interaction. The findings may inform integrated prevention strategies for PONV after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07631910, identifier NCT07631910.

articles.title: Multi-target effects of bergapten in a vitro periodontitis-mimicking model: suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress while promoting osteogenesis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bergapten (BG) is a natural furanocoumarin found in various botanical drugs including Citrus bergamia, Angelica archangelica, and Citrus medica, and it's a bioactive constituent of Peucedanum guangxiense, an indigenous species in Guangxi, China. Although BG exhibits anti-inflammatory and osteoprotective properties, its effects relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment remains unexplored. METHODS: This study integrated network analysis with in vitro experimental validation to investigate the multi-target effects of BG in a Porphyromonas gingivalis lipopolysaccharide (P.g-LPS) -induced periodontitis-mimicking in vitro model. RESULTS: Network analysis and molecular docking identified the PI3K/Akt pathway as a candidate pathway, along with predicted binding to CAT, BMP-2, TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β. BG at concentration of 5-30 μM did not reduce cell viability in human periodontal ligament stem cells (h-PDLSCs) or RAW264 .7 macrophages under the tested conditions. BG at concentrations of 7.5-30 μM directly promoted osteogenic differentiation of h-PDLSCs beyond baseline levels in the normal-mimicking microenvironment, as evidenced by increased ALP activity, mineralization, and expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2, COL-I, OCN, and OPN). Under inflammatory conditions, BG reduced intracellular oxidative activity across concentrations of 7.5-30 μM, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), down-regulated M1 macrophages polarization associated markers (iNOS, CD86) and NF-κB components (IκBα, p65), while up-regulating anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-4, IL-10), M2 macrophages polarization-associated markers (Arg-1, CD206) and antioxidant genes (HO-1,CAT, SOD). Moreover, BG-treated macrophages conditioned medium partially rescued the osteogenic capacity of h-PDLSCs in inflammation condition, though not to the level of the normal control. The effects might associate with increased phosphorylation levels of PI3K and Akt, and with decreased mRNA expression of NF-κB pathway components. CONCLUSION: Collectively, BG was associated with multi-modal effects relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment, including alleviating oxidative stress, suppressing NF-κB driven inflammation, promoting PI3K/Akt associated osteogenesis, and shifting macrophage polarization-associated markers toward an M2-like profile. Our in vitro findings suggest that BG possess multi-modal activities relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment, warranting further in vivo investigation to assess its pharmacological relevance.

articles.title: Multi-omics identifies PCK1-associated immunometabolic regulation underlying the protective effects of sinomenine in vascular dementia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular dementia (VaD) is one of the major causes of cognitive impairment among older adults. However, effective treatments that can modify the progression of the disease are still lacking. Emerging evidence indicates that metabolic remodeling in microglia influences inflammatory responses during vascular brain injury. Microglial immunometabolic regulation has therefore been proposed as an important contributor to the pathogenesis of vascular dementia (VaD). METHODS: Transcriptomic integration, WGCNA, network pharmacology, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing were combined to identify disease-associated microglial alterations and potential targets involved in sinomenine (SIN)-mediated regulation. The interaction between SIN and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1) was investigated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. The biological effects of SIN were then validated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglia. RESULTS: Integrated analyses highlighted PCK1 as a potential mediator associated with SIN-induced metabolic regulation in VaD. snRNA-seq demonstrated expansion of metabolically stressed microglial states accompanied by PCK1-related metabolic alterations. Stable binding between SIN and PCK1 was supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia, SIN suppressed inflammatory activation, restored PCK1 expression, attenuated inflammation-associated metabolic remodeling, improved cellular bioenergetics, and modulated metabolic redox-related parameters. SIN also enhanced adaptive stress responses through regulation of CRYAB, APOD, and HSPH1. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings suggest that SIN alleviates VaD-associated microglial dysfunction by modulating PCK1-associated immunometabolic alterations. They expand the current understanding of the pharmacological actions of SIN and highlight microglial immunometabolic regulation as a potential therapeutic target for VaD.

articles.title: Berbamine exerts anti-breast-cancer effects in association with autophagy-related responses and PI3K/Akt1/mTOR signaling.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and effective, well-tolerated therapeutic strategies are needed. Berbamine (BBM), a natural bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid, has anticancer activity, but its effects on autophagy- and lysosome-related processes in breast cancer remain incompletely understood.
