METHODS: In this single-center, prospective observational cohort study, 93 patients (control group, n = 65; trilaciclib group, n = 28) enrolled between October 2023 and March 2026 were analyzed. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Binary, longitudinal, and survival outcomes were analyzed using IPTW-weighted Firth-penalized logistic regression, weighted generalized estimating equations, and weighted Cox models, respectively, with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: After weighting, baseline characteristics were well balanced (all standardized mean differences <0.10). Compared with control, the trilaciclib group had lower weighted incidences of grade 3-4 CIM (3.0% vs. 31.2%; odds ratio [OR] 0.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.48; FDR-adjusted P = 0.007), grade 3-4 neutropenia (3.0% vs. 28.3%; OR 0.12, 95% CI: 0.01-0.55; FDR-adjusted P = 0.010), and grade 3-4 anemia (0.0% vs. 17.3%; OR 0.08, 95% CI: <0.01-0.67; FDR-adjusted P = 0.030). Grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia, severe neutropenia, and febrile neutropenia did not differ significantly. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) use was also lower in the trilaciclib group (34.4% vs. 79.7% and 3.7% vs. 29.6%; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001 and P = 0.010, respectively). Overall survival, disease-free survival, and pathologic outcomes did not differ significantly. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or noninferiority. CONCLUSION: In this small, single-center cohort, trilaciclib use was associated with lower grade 3-4 myelosuppression and less hematopoietic supportive care. No statistically significant unfavorable differences in pathologic or survival outcomes were observed; however, equivalence cannot be inferred. These results are hypothesis-generating and require validation in randomized trials.

articles.title: Hydroxytyrosol attenuates intimal hyperplasia in in vitro and ex vivo human saphenous vein models: association with Akt and Nrf2/HO-1 signalling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous intimal hyperplasia remains a major cause of saphenous vein graft failure following coronary artery bypass grafting Current antiproliferative strategies often impair endothelial cell function, exacerbating vascular injury. Hydroxytyrosol (HT), a bioactive olive phenolic compound, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its coordinated effects on vascular smooth muscle cells and ECs remain unclear. METHODS: Primary human saphenous vein-derived SMCs and ECs were exposed to graded concentrations of HT to evaluate cell viability, proliferation, migration, chemotaxis, and signalling responses. A human saphenous vein ring (hSVR) culture model was used to investigate the effects of HT on spontaneous ex vivo intimal hyperplasia. RESULTS: HT (20-320 μM) significantly inhibited PDGF-BB-induced SMC proliferation, migration, and chemotaxis accompanied by reduced Akt signalling. In contrast, HT at concentrations ≤50 μM did not produce a statistically significant reduction in EC viability, proliferation, and migration while activating the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway. In the ex vivo hSVR model, 50 μM HT reduced intimal thickness by 45.2% and significantly attenuated neointimal cell proliferation at day 21. HT also suppressed Akt activation, enhanced HO-1 expression, and reduced vimentin expression, consistent with attenuation of vascular remodeling. Attempts to evaluate re-endothelialization were inconclusive because seeded ECs failed to establish continuous luminal coverage in the ex vivo model. CONCLUSION: Hydroxytyrosol selectively inhibits SMC activation while preserving endothelial homeostasis associated with differential modulation of the Akt and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways. These findings demonstrate that HT effectively attenuates intimal hyperplasia in a human ex vivo vein model and support its potential as an adjunctive strategy for improving vein graft patency. Further studies using perfused vascular systems or in vivo models are required to determine its effects on endothelial repair and re-endothelialisation.

articles.title: Differences in cytotoxicity and apparent extracellular glucose utilisation among sequentially prepared Cinnamomum cassia stem-bark extracts in basal and palmitate-associated C2C12 myotubes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cinnamomum cassia bark has a documented history of use in traditional medicine and food-medicine practices associated with diabetes and metabolic disorders. This study compared preliminary phytochemical fingerprints, MTT metabolic-viability responses and apparent extracellular glucose utilisation among sequentially prepared stem-bark extracts. METHODS: Authenticated, vouchered stem bark was extracted sequentially with n-hexane, ethyl acetate, ethanol and water. Extracts were examined by thin-layer chromatography and qualitative phytochemical screening. MTT reduction was assessed after 72 h. Residual extracellular glucose was measured after 180 min, and apparent extracellular glucose utilisation was calculated as 15 mmol/L minus the residual concentration. This endpoint does not directly measure membrane glucose transport or intracellular utilisation. Three independent experiments were conducted in technical triplicate, with technical wells averaged within experiments. The retained non-insulin basal well-level values were reconstructed from reported summary statistics and were therefore treated descriptively; the palmitate-associated dataset was analysed using independent-experiment means. RESULTS: The sequential fractions showed different preliminary fingerprints and concentration-related MTT profiles. Within each palmitate-associated extract series, one or more concentrations showed greater apparent extracellular glucose utilisation than the concurrent palmitate-only control; no formal comparison among extracts was performed. CONCLUSION: Sequential fractions showed different MTT and apparent extracellular glucose-utilisation profiles. The endpoint is indirect, was not normalised to concurrent viability or cell number, and may be affected by vehicle or assay interference. Quantitative cinnamaldehyde and coumarin characterisation was not performed. The findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish glucose uptake, GLUT4 activation, insulin sensitisation, extract superiority, therapeutic efficacy or in vivo safety.

articles.title: Extending the high-throughput toxicokinetics R package to include brain and adipose compartments.
articles.abstract: Chemical risk assessment has traditionally been performed based on in vivo studies. These studies have limited throughput, consequently leading to limited toxicity information for the majority of chemicals in industrial and commercial use. In addition, the translation from animal to human effects can be challenging. To increase human-relevant toxicity knowledge, high-throughput in vitro approaches have been developed. However, one challenge in employing these assays for hazard and risk assessment is the translation of in vitro bioactive concentrations to in vivo doses and internal tissue concentrations. To improve decision-making in chemical risk assessment, as well as drug discovery for humans, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has developed a simple physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK) model as part of the High-throughput Toxicokinetics open-source R package (httk). In this study, the PBTK model was extended to include compartments for the brain and adipose tissues. The model incorporates a blood-brain barrier to control chemical penetration and disposition, which is essential for predicting neurotoxicity. The integration of an adipose tissue compartment further enables the prediction of bioaccumulation, particularly for lipophilic chemicals. The model's performance was evaluated by comparing predicted chemical concentrations against experimental data from both oral and intravenous routes. This PBTK model extends the applicability of httk to allow for assessing potential neurotoxicity and chronic exposure to lipophilic chemicals and better evaluate chemical pharmacokinetics. Moreover, this PBTK model can act as a tool for optimizing dosages and other study parameters to reduce and refine the design of in vivo studies.

articles.title: Defining competency frameworks for undergraduate and graduate pharmacology education in Canada.
articles.abstract: Pharmacology education in Canada spans multiple institutions and programs and is increasingly integrated with other disciplines. While this diversity is a strength, the absence of a national consensus on the core competencies required for graduation raises concerns about consistency across programs, accreditation, and potential gaps in knowledge and skills. To address these gaps, the Canadian Society of Pharmacology and Therapeutics (CSPT) launched an initiative to establish national competency frameworks for undergraduate and graduate pre-professional pharmacology programs. Using an exploratory sequential mixed methods design, an initial list of knowledge, skill, and attitude statements was developed through a literature review and iterative input from CSPT Education Committee members and participants in the 2024 CSPT Meeting Education Workshop. Semi-structured focus groups and interviews were then conducted with pharmacology professionals from the academic, public, and private sectors to explore their views on the core competencies for pharmacology graduates and to gather feedback on the initial list. Inductive content analysis revealed strong cross-sector agreement that the principles of drug action and therapeutic response are essential for pharmacology graduates. Academic sector participants emphasized pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics as core knowledge at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Private sector participants prioritized laboratory and regulatory competencies, and public sector participants emphasized interdisciplinary collaboration. A modified Delphi questionnaire with national panellists produced lists of 27 and 55 statements for the undergraduate and graduate levels, respectively. Consensus statements were then restructured into competencies, incorporating the level of knowledge or skill acquisition rated by panellists for each academic level. This yielded an undergraduate framework of 12 key and 32 enabling competencies, and a graduate framework of 17 key and 58 enabling competencies, representing the first consensus-based, level-specific competency frameworks for pharmacology programs in Canada. These frameworks will guide curriculum design, professional preparation, and pharmacology training needs.

articles.title: A multi-dimensional comparative evaluation of ten injectable neuroprotective agents for acute ischemic stroke based on the Chinese guideline for drug selection.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To conduct a multi-dimensional, comparative evaluation of ten commonly used injectable neuroprotective agents to provide an evidence-based reference for rational drug selection and clinical application in treating acute ischemic stroke (AIS). METHODS: In accordance with A Quick Guideline for Drug Evaluation and Selection in Chinese Medical Institutions (3rd Edition), this study quantitatively assessed ten injectable neuroprotective agents. The evaluation utilized a comprehensive, evidence-based approach, sourcing data from drug package inserts, clinical guidelines, and multiple scientific databases. Each drug was scored across five dimensions: pharmaceutical properties, efficacy, safety, cost-effectiveness, and other relevant attributes. RESULTS: The comprehensive evaluation yielded a ranked list of the neuroprotective agents. The top three scoring drugs were Butylphthalide and Sodium Chloride Injection (70.17 points), Urinary Kallidinogenase for Injection (69.21 points), and Edaravone and Dexborneol Concentrated Solution for Injection (67.82 points). Conversely, Citicoline Sodium Injection received the lowest score (32.97 points), primarily due to insufficient evidence supporting its clinical efficacy. Stratified recommendation levels were strictly defined based on composite scores: only Butylphthalide and Sodium Chloride Injection met the threshold for the Strongly Recommended category, while Urinary Kallidinogenase for Injection and Edaravone and Dexborneol Concentrated Solution for Injection were classified as Weakly Recommended agents. CONCLUSION: This study provides a quantitative, multi-dimensional ranking that identifies only Butylphthalide and Sodium Chloride Injection as the strongly recommended neuroprotective agent, with Urinary Kallidinogenase and Edaravone Dexborneol serving as weakly recommended alternatives for AIS within the Chinese healthcare context. These results offer a direct, evidence-based tool for hospital pharmacy committees to optimize drug formularies and for clinicians to make more standardized treatment decisions. By bridging the evidence gap between various agents, this evaluation framework supports more rational drug application and helps reduce variability in clinical neuroprotective therapy in Chinese medical institutions.

articles.title: A four-herb topical formula attenuates psoriasis-like skin inflammation by suppressing IL-17-mediated inflammation and pathogenic γδT17 cell infiltration.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease driven by dysregulation of IL-17-mediated immune responses. Current topical therapies, including corticosteroids, are limited by long-term side effects, creating demand for safer alternatives. DH-YH is a novel four-herb Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formula derived from Duhuo Jisheng Tang, comprising Angelica pubescens, Gentiana macrophylla, Taxillus chinensis, and Paeonia lactiflora. Based on an initial clinical observation of improvement following topical DH-YH treatment in a patient with psoriasis, this study investigated its immunomodulatory effects in psoriasis-related models. METHODS: The anti-inflammatory effects of DH-YH were assessed in vitro using IL-17A-stimulated human keratinocytes (HaCaT cells) and LPS-activated bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) and RAW264.7 macrophages. The effects on T-cell polarization were evaluated in murine splenic CD4+ T cells differentiated toward Th1, Th2, and Th17 lineages. In vivo, an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model (BALB/c, n = 5/group) was used to evaluate topical DH-YH ointment. Skin histopathology (H&E staining) and multi-organ flow cytometric analysis (skin, spleen, and lymph nodes) were performed to assess epidermal thickness, inflammatory infiltration, and immune cell subset frequencies. RESULTS: Topical DH-YH ointment markedly improved psoriatic lesions in a clinical case without hepatorenal toxicity. In vitro, DH-YH dose-dependently suppressed IL-8 secretion in IL-17A-stimulated HaCaT cells and inhibited TNF-α and IL-6 production in LPS-activated BMDCs. DH-YH also significantly reduced Th17 and Th2 cell differentiation without affecting cell viability. In the IMQ-induced mouse model, topical DH-YH significantly reduced epidermal thickness and dermal inflammatory cell infiltration. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that DH-YH specifically decreased the proportions of CD45+, CD3+, γδT, and γδT17 cells in lesional skin. CONCLUSION: DH-YH attenuates psoriasis-related inflammatory responses across multiple cellular and immune components, including keratinocyte inflammatory responses, BMDC cytokine production, T helper cell differentiation, and γδT17 cell accumulation.

articles.title: GPR84 inhibition attenuates sepsis-associated acute lung injury and preserves pulmonary endothelial barrier function associated with YY1 suppression.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dysregulation of the pulmonary endothelial barrier precipitates the edema and inflammation central to sepsis-associated acute lung injury (ALI). Although the G-protein-coupled receptor GPR84 orchestrates various inflammatory responses, its specific contribution to maintaining microvascular integrity during sepsis remains largely undefined. METHODS: We explored the therapeutic efficacy of GPR84 inhibition using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse model and LPS-challenged lung microvascular endothelial cells (MLMECs). RESULTS: Pulmonary GPR84 expression surged following septic insult, and its pharmacological blockade via selective inhibitors (GLPG1205 or TUG-2181) effectively mitigated alveolar damage. This intervention restored respiratory mechanics-including peak expiratory flow (PEF) and airway resistance (Raw)-and decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine concentrations (TNF-α, IL-6, CXCL15) within the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Furthermore, GPR84 inhibition curtailed vascular protein leakage and preserved Occludin expression across both experimental models. At the molecular level, GPR84 signaling appeared to facilitate the LPS-induced upregulation of the transcription factor YY1. In cultured endothelial cells, the barrier-protective effect of GPR84 inhibition was diminished by YY1 overexpression, indicating a functional role for YY1 in this in vitro system. DISCUSSION: Collectively, these results suggest that GPR84 inhibition attenuates sepsis-associated ALI in association with YY1 suppression in vivo, identifying GPR84 as a candidate therapeutic target warranting further preclinical and clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic determinants, clinical efficacy, and safety of teicoplanin in adults: a correlative analysis of plasma concentration and treatment outcomes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) method for the determination of plasma teicoplanin concentrations, identify factors influencing teicoplanin exposure in adult patients, and assess its clinical efficacy and safety. METHODS: A cohort of 125 adult patients who received teicoplanin therapy at the Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University between June 2022 and March 2023 were retrospectively enrolled. Trough plasma teicoplanin concentrations were determined using a validated HPLC method with quetiapine fumarate as the internal standard. Clinical data, including demographic characteristics, infection type, laboratory parameters, and treatment outcomes, were collected. Logistic regression analyses was conducted to evaluate the clinical efficacy of teicoplanin, attainment of target trough concentrations, and factors associated with these outcomes. RESULTS: The HPLC method demonstrated high specificity, satisfactory linearity over the concentration range of 1.5625-100 μg/mL, and acceptable precision, recovery, and stability. Under the standard dosing regimen, only 45.6% of patients achieved a teicoplanin trough concentration (Cmin) > 10 mg/L. The overall clinical efficacy rate was 87.20%, and the bacteriological clearance rate was 82.61%. Adverse events included renal injury (8.80%) and hepatic injury (1.60%), with renal injury occurring more frequently in patients with higher Cmin values. Bivariate analysis showed that teicoplanin trough concentrations were significantly associated with creatinine clearance (CrCL) and plasma albumin levels. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCL <30 mL min-1) were more likely to achieve the target trough concentration. In addition, the incidence of renal injury increased significantly when the trough concentration exceeded 20 mg/L. CONCLUSION: A reliable, accurate, and reproducible HPLC method for the therapeutic drug monitoring of teicoplanin was successfully developed and validated. Application of the validated method presented substantial interindividual variability in teicoplanin plasma concentrations, with CrCL and plasma albumin identified as major factors associated with drug exposure. These findings provide a reliable analytical foundation for future studies of individualized teicoplanin dosing. However, given the retrospective observational design and the absence of real-time therapeutic drug monitoring-guided dose adjustment, the observed associations between trough concentrations and clinical outcomes should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than causal.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of combination of ezetimibe and sericin against lead-induced neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Chronic exposure to environmental pollutants, particularly heavy metals, has become a global health concern, reducing longevity. Among these, lead (Pb2+) is associated with neurobehavioral, neurodevelopmental, and neuropsychological impairments. Consequently, growing interest focuses on pharmacological and natural agents that restore neurotrophic signaling. Therefore, this study investigates neuroprotective effect of ezetimibe, an anti-hyperlipidemic agent, and sericin, a natural protein, in Pb2+-induced neurotoxicity in rats. Adult Wistar rats were divided into seven groups: control, lead acetate (PbAc2; 50 mg/kg), ezetimibe (10 and 20 mg/kg), sericin (200 and 400 mg/kg), and a combination of ezetimibe (10 mg/kg) and sericin (200 mg/kg) with PbAc2. PbAc2 was administered for 55 days, while ezetimibe and sericin treatment was initiated on days 29-55. Behavioral assessments, including grip strength, open field test, and Morris water maze test, were performed. On day 56, animals were sacrificed, and hippocampal tissues were collected for neurochemical (GABA, GAD1, and dopamine) and mitochondrial complex 3 estimation, along with hippocampal histology. The qRT-PCR (Bax, Bcl2, caspase - 3, CREB, BDNF), western blot (IGF-1R, GLP-1R, PI3K, pAkt) were performed. The results demonstrated that PbAc2 exposure induced behavioral deficits, neurotransmitter imbalance, disrupted mitochondrial-associated apoptotic pathway, and impaired neurotrophin signaling. Contrarily, ezetimibe and sericin, individually and in combination, significantly attenuated neurobehavioral impairments, restored neurochemical levels, improved mitochondrial complex III activity, suppressed apoptotic signaling, and preserved hippocampal histoarchitecture and enhanced synaptic plasticity through involvement of IGF-1R/GLP-1R signaling pathway. These findings suggest that ezetimibe and sericin, in combination, represent promising therapeutic candidates for mitigating PbAc2-induced neurotoxicity.

articles.title: Cannabis-based medicinal products for post-traumatic stress disorder: a two-year prospective analysis from the UK medical cannabis registry.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterised by persistent psychological symptoms following exposure to trauma. Cannabis-based medicinal products (CBMPs) have promising therapeutic potential. However, there is a paucity of long-term studies investigating their use. OBJECTIVES: This prospective case series aimed to assess changes in patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and the prevalence of adverse events in patients prescribed CBMPs for PTSD. METHODS: Patients enrolled on the United Kingdom Medical Cannabis Registry for PTSD were included. Changes in PROMs (Impact of Events Scale-Revised (IES-R), Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale (SQS) and EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level questionnaire (EQ-5D-5​L)) were assessed from baseline up to 24 months. RESULTS: In total, 446 patients were included, of which 75.11% (n = 335) were already using cannabis before starting treatment. Mean IES-R, GAD-7, SQS and EQ-5D-5​L scores improved relative to baseline at all follow-up times (p < 0.001). At 24 months, 64.57% (n = 288) of IES-R data were imputed. The mean IES-R fell from 59.58 ± 15.93 at baseline to 36.91 ± 18.56 at 24 months, with 55.38% (n = 247) of patients continuing to meet the DSM-IV threshold for PTSD at 24 months. Seventy-five patients (16.82%) reported at least one adverse event. Of 578 events, 83 (14.36%) were severe, and 2 (0.35%) life-threatening or disabling. CONCLUSION: In this uncontrolled case series, CBMP treatment was associated with improvements in mean PTSD symptom, anxiety, sleep, and health-related quality of life scores. However, the improvement was concentrated within the first month and then plateaued. The observational design, high attrition, and reliance on imputed data preclude any inference of efficacy or causality.

articles.title: Degradation-Driven Implications for the Pharmacology and Risk Profile of Fexofenadine.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Understanding a drug's degradation profile is essential for ensuring its stability, efficacy, and safety. This minireview summarizes the pharmacological characteristics of fexofenadine and predicts its degradation pathways, with an emphasis on quality assessment and regulatory implications. METHODS: To build on the outlined objectives, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Scopus using keywords related to fexofenadine's pharmacology, chemical structure, and degradation mechanisms. Of 368 records identified, 52 studies met the inclusion criteria and were critically analyzed. RESULTS: Following this analysis, it was found that fexofenadine is susceptible to photolysis, hydrolysis, and N-nitrosation processes. DISCUSSION: Fexofenadine's vulnerabilities, which are corroborated by forced degradation studies, may compromise its stability and lead to nitrosamine formation. Notably, the drug is primarily excreted unchanged, indicating minimal metabolic transformation. Predicted metabolic routes include aromatic hydroxylation, Ndealkylation, and piperidine ring opening; however, its high polarity favors renal elimination. Phase II conjugation, particularly glucuronidation, may further contribute to its clearance and the absence of detectable metabolites. In addition, nanoformulations have been shown to enhance fexofenadine's stability, bioavailability, and therapeutic performance. CONCLUSION: Further investigation into fexofenadine's stability is critical for optimizing formulation strategies, guiding quality control, and mitigating degradation-related risks. Theoretical and experimental insights can strengthen regulatory compliance and ensure sustained drug safety.

articles.title: Ligand-modified Lipid-based Drug Delivery Vehicles for the Selective Targeting of Cancerous Cells.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy is widely recognized as the mainstay of cancer therapy; however, its lack of specificity and off-target toxicities limit therapeutic success. The lipid-based nanocarriers with targeting ligands such as folic acid, transferrin, aptamers, and antibodies are widely recognized as effective for cancer cell targeting. However, no ligand-modified lipid-based system has reached regulatory approval despite three decades of preclinical development. This review synthesizes and evaluates mechanistic, computational, and translational aspects of ligand-modified lipid nanocarriers. The review discusses lipid drug delivery systems in cancer and targeting strategies, mainly focusing on active targeting by ligands. The ligands are compared against standardized criteria, revealing no single class dominates but rather a balance of competing properties. The enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect is examined against clinical evidence. The barriers for ligand-modified lipid-based nanoparticles that can affect the ligand targeting efficiency are discussed. Given the redirected accumulation of LNPs in the liver, which leads to hepatic tropism, approaches such as biomimetics and stealth ligand modification are discussed as strategies to prolong circulation and improve therapeutic efficacy. Furthermore, applications of artificial intelligence to ligand-modified lipid nanoparticles are reviewed, with identification of gaps in application in ligand-modified LNPs. Clinically, FDA- and EMA-approved lipid formulations validate translational feasibility, though ligand-modified systems remain challenging due to manufacturing complexity and regulatory hurdles. This review uniquely integrates mechanistic, translational, and computational perspectives of ligand-modified lipid-based nanoparticle systems to bridge laboratory and preclinical innovation with clinical feasibility in cancer therapeutics.

articles.title: Antitumor potentials of matrine; molecular and cellular mechanisms and interactions with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer continues to be the second leading cause of death globally and poses a significant public health issue. There is growing research and clinical interest in natural compounds that possess strong anticancer properties. Matrine, a quinolizidine alkaloid sourced from the traditional Chinese herbal remedy Sophora flavescens, shows a wide array of pharmacological actions, including antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antiarrhythmic, hepatoprotective, antibacterial, and analgesic effects. OBJECTIVES: This summary outlines the antitumor mechanisms of matrine, focusing on its interactions with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment. It also covers matrine's chemical properties, challenges in clinical translation, and future research directions. METHODS: This study conducted a narrative review using searches across the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. The primary keywords included matrine, its structural class, and its antitumor and immunomodulatory mechanisms. The literature reviewed spanned from 2001 to 2026. RESULTS: Matrine has shown a range of drug-related effects., encompassing properties such as antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antiarrhythmic, and hepatoprotective, antibacterial, and analgesic properties. Recent research has indicated that matrine exhibits potential anti-cancer properties via various molecular mechanisms, including the capacity to suppress the growth of cancer cells, trigger cell cycle arrest, stimulate the death of cancer cells, hinder angiogenesis, prevention of cancer invasion and metastasis, overcome multidrug resistance, lessen or prevent the harmful effects linked to chemotherapy or radiotherapy when used in combination with different chemotherapeutic drugs, and also exert anticancer effects through its interaction with immune cells. Structure-activity data point to the D-ring lactam as a key determinant of bioactivity, while nanoparticle-based delivery and combination regimens appear promising for addressing matrine's pharmacokinetic limitations. Clinical evidence, however, remains limited. CONCLUSIONS: Matrine is a multi-target natural compound and may have direct antitumor and immunomodulatory capabilities. Existing preclinical studies have identified that matrine is a promising candidate for cancer therapy development. Independent validation of mechanisms, chemical optimization, and specific delivery technology, along with human pharmacokinetic and safety studies, are all key to applying matrine for clinical treatment.

articles.title: Case report: Fournier's gangrene occurring after inavolisib-induced hyperglycemia in a patient with metastatic breast cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inavolisib is a selective inhibitor and degrader of mutant phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase alpha (PI3Kα) approved for PIK3CA-mutated, hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, and hyperglycemia is its most frequent class effect. Fournier's gangrene is an uncommon necrotizing infection of the perineal region with reported mortality of 20%-40%. Necrotizing infections have only exceptionally been described in the context of PI3K inhibitor therapy, but to our knowledge Fournier's gangrene has not been previously reported with any PI3Kα inhibitor. CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old woman with PIK3CA-mutated metastatic breast carcinoma, obesity, and impaired fasting glucose without diabetes, receiving fulvestrant, palbociclib and inavolisib, developed grade 3 hyperglycemia refractory to metformin and rapid escalation of basal insulin, with a peak plasma glucose of 623 mg/dL. Inavolisib was interrupted and briefly reintroduced at a reduced dose, whereupon hyperglycemia recurred. Forty-seven days after inavolisib initiation, she was admitted to the intensive care unit with septic shock associated with necrosis of the skin over the perianal region and both buttocks. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography, polymicrobial cultures, and histology confirmed the diagnosis of Fournier's gangrene. She required surgical debridements and fecal diversion, gradually recovering from the infection and undergoing reconstructive coverage of the gluteal defect. Eight months after presentation, the defect remained durably healed, while the metastatic breast cancer progressed and required two subsequent lines of systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: This report describes the occurrence of inavolisib-induced hyperglycemia and a subsequent life-threatening necrotizing infection. Our findings support individualized metabolic and infectious risk stratification before PI3Kα inhibition and urgent evaluation of perineal symptoms in patients who develop severe or refractory hyperglycemia under these targeted therapies.

articles.title: An effective approach for the management of men's sexual dysfunction via local administration of Sildenafil/cyclodextrin-loaded hydrogels.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to enhance the bioavailability of Sildenafil via cyclodextrin inclusion complexation and to formulate various hydrogel systems containing modified Sildenafil as an alternative, safe treatment for erectile dysfunction. SIGNIFICANCE: Oral administration of Sildenafil is accompanied by severe hypotension, making this drug contraindicated for patients with cardiac dysfunction, which may lead to fatal acute and severe hypotension. Therefore, topical and local administration is considered an option to avoid side effects accompanying oral administration. METHODS: The current work was divided into three distinct segments. First, we enhanced the solubility of sildenafil by forming and characterizing inclusion complexes with hydroxypropyl-β-CD. Secondly, hydrogels were prepared and characterized using different gelling agents, including Carbopol 940, HPMC, and Gelatin. Lastly, the selected hydrogel system was utilized for the in vivo application in participants (n = 60). The gel formulation was applied locally on the penis 0.5 h before intercourse, and both intravaginal latency time (IVLT) and International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) were monitored before and after drug application. Besides, irritation studies were conducted on rat models. RESULTS: The drug solubility and dissolution rate were markedly improved via inclusion complexation with cyclodextrin. Also, the medicated hydrogel formulations exhibited good consistency, spreadability, and homogeneity. Notably, the gel composed of HPMC, loaded with modified Sildenafil, demonstrated the fastest release rate compared to the other gelling agents. The in vivo results revealed a remarkable improvement in both erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation parameters (IVLT and IIEF-5). Also, the results showed that there is no sign of irritation upon application. CONCLUSION: The modified Sildenafil hydrogel is an alternative and safe therapy for patients suffering from erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation since this route of administration avoids severe risks accompanying oral administration.

articles.title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Extracts and Active Biomolecules of Morinda officinalis How: A Review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Global population aging and the rising burden of immunosenescencerelated disorders have created an urgent need for safe, low-toxicity immunomodulators suitable for middleaged and elderly populations. Morinda officinalis How (MO, called "Ba-Ji-Tian" in China), a traditional Chinese kidney-tonifying herb, has shown promising immunomodulatory activity. This review aims to integrate current knowledge on the multidimensional immunomodulatory functions and regulatory networks of MO extracts and their major active biomolecules and summarize their mechanistic contributions in immune-related diseases. METHODS: Peer-reviewed literature published over the past decade was comprehensively searched and systematically appraised to evaluate the in vitro and in vivo immunomodulatory effects of MO extracts and their major active constituents, including MO polysaccharides, oligosaccharides, iridoid glycosides, anthraquinones, and sterols. RESULTS: Accumulating evidence indicates that MO exerts bidirectional immunoregulation by modulating cytokine secretion, promoting the proliferation and activation of immune cells including lymphocytes and macrophages, and increasing immune organ indices. Its representative compounds, such as monotropein, rubiadin, physcion, daucosterol, and stigmasterol, contribute to these effects and help alleviate aging-related chronic inflammatory diseases. DISCUSSION: MO extracts and active biomolecules exhibit marked immunomodulatory properties. However, these findings vary across experimental models and doses, and the molecular mechanism remains incompletely defined. Standardized extracts and mechanism-oriented studies are therefore needed to support translational development. CONCLUSION: MO and its active biomolecules represent promising, mildly acting immunomodulators with considerable potential for clinical application in aging-related immune dysfunction.

articles.title: Jiangtang Pill for Type 2 Diabetes: Network Pharmacology and Transcriptomics.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study computationally explores the polypharmacological mechanisms of Jiangtang Pill (JTP) in treating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) using an integrated in silico approach. METHODS: Active compounds of JTP and predicted pharmacological targets were extracted from databases. Protein-protein interaction networks identified core hubs, which were intersected with DEGs from a T2DM transcriptomic dataset (GSE15932). Functional mechanisms were evaluated via GO and KEGG analyses. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT. Molecular docking and 100-ns Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to evaluate the predicted binding interactions and dynamic behavior of key ligand-protein complexes. RESULTS: AKT1, MAPK3, STAT3, and TNF emerged as candidate targets supported by the integrated network and transcriptomic analyses. Functional enrichment highlighted the PI3K-Akt, AGE-RAGE, and MAPK pathways. CIBERSORT analysis indicated a lower estimated abundance of CD4+ memory activated T cells in T2DM, which was inversely associated with the expression of selected targets. The 100-ns MD simulations showed that the four ligand-protein complexes remained dynamically associated throughout the trajectories, with distinct RMSD, RMSF, compactness, and hydrogen-bonding profiles for β-sitosterol and kaempferol. DISCUSSION: By integrating network pharmacology, clinical transcriptomics, and structural analyses, this study supports a hypothesis that JTP may influence metabolic and immune-related pathways involved in T2DM. CONCLUSION: These findings provide a testable computational framework for the potential multi-target actions of JTP and warrant further experimental validation.

articles.title: The cyto-genotoxic potential of dibutyl phthalate promotes DNA damage and cellular stress with altered DNA repair gene expression in Madin-Darby Bovine Kidney (MDBK) cells.
articles.abstract: Dibutyl phthalate (DBP) is a widely used plasticizer and endocrine-disrupting chemical frequently detected in polyvinyl chloride (PVC) consumer products and environmental matrices. Although there is growing evidence of its toxicological effects, data on its cyto-genotoxic potential and the resulting molecular responses in bovine renal epithelial cells are limited. The present study investigated the cytotoxic, genotoxic, and chromosomal destabilizing effects of DBP in Madin-Darby Bovine Kidney (MDBK) cells and examined the transcriptional responses of the DNA damage-associated genes OGG1 and HPRT1. MTT assay was used to determine cell viability after exposing cells to different DBP concentrations ranging from 5 to 200 µM. Cells were then treated with 25, 50 and 75 µM DBP for the alkaline comet assay, micronucleus assay and quantitative real-time PCR analysis, based on the estimated LC₅₀ value. DBP induced a concentration-dependent reduction in cell viability, with an LC₅₀ of 50 µM after 24 h of exposure. Significant dose-dependent increases (p < 0.05) were observed in DNA damage index, comet tail DNA percentage, and genomic instability index. Similarly, micronucleus and binucleated cell frequencies, and cytostasis increased significantly, whereas cytokinesis-block proliferation index (CBPI) decreased with increasing DBP concentration. The highest tested concentration (75 µM) elicited cyto-genotoxic responses comparable to the positive control group. Gene expression analysis showed that both OGG1 (5.33-fold) and HPRT1 (6.57-fold) were elevated, with higher DBP concentrations leading to increased gene expression. These findings highlight that DBP induces concentration-dependent cyto-genotoxicity and transcriptional alterations in MDBK cells, underscoring the need for safer plasticizer alternatives.

articles.title: The inhibition of tricin on human liver cytochrome P450 enzymes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tricin has attracted increasing attention due to its diverse pharmacological properties, highlighting its considerable potential for clinical application. However, its potential for drug-drug interactions (DDIs) and its inhibitory effects on human cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the effect of tricin on CYP450s. METHODS: The inhibitory effect of tricin on CYP450s was evaluated by an in vitro study using human pooled live microsomes (HLMs). Tricin, CYP450 enzymes, and the corresponding substrates were co-incubated with HLMs using a NADPH-generating system, and the HLMs incubated without tricin or positive inhibitors served as the negative control. Corresponding inhibitory parameters were obtained by incubating tricin (0-100 µM) with the specific substrates at different concentrations. RESULTS: Tricin showed a selective inhibitory effect on the activities of CYP1A2, 2D6, and 3A4, with the IC50 values of 12.760 µM, 14.050 µM, and 6.925 µM for CYP3A4 with testosterone as substrate, and 8.070 µM for CYP3A4 with midazolam as substrate, respectively. It was revealed that tricin competitively inhibited the activities of CYP1A2 (Ki=5.641 µM) and 2D6 (Ki=6.247 µM) while non-competitively inhibited the activity of CYP3A4 (Ki=2.876 µM). The activity of CYP3A4 was also inhibited by tricin in a time-dependent inhibition (TDI) manner with a KI of 1.418 µM and a Kinact of 0.029 min⁻¹. CONCLUSIONS: In vitro HLM study indicated the competitive inhibition of tricin on CYP1A2 and 2D6, while non-competitive inhibition and TDI on CYP3A4, thereby informing its potential for clinical drug interactions. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Trastuzumab-conjugated Docetaxel-loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carriers for Gastric Cancer.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancers overexpressing human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) (10-20% of cases) are often associated with aggressive disease and poorer clinical outcomes. Trastuzumab (TZM), a HER2-specific monoclonal antibody, and docetaxel (DTX), a microtubule-stabilizing agent, are established therapies for gastric cancer, with their combination demonstrating efficacy in HER2-positive cases. Nanotechnology enables co-administration of antibodies and drugs, improving control over delivery and prolonging retention within tumors. This study aimed to develop DTX-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (NLC) covalently conjugated to TZM for local treatment of HER2-positive gastric cancer. Carbodiimide-mediated conjugation was verified by light-scattering and spectroscopic techniques, and the bound antibody was estimated using a colorimetric assay. The conjugated NLC were characterized for their physicochemical properties, stability, drug incorporation, morphology, in vitro release, and in vitro cytotoxicity against AGS (HER2-negative) and NCI-N87 (HER2-positive) cells. The results suggest successful TZM conjugation, yielding stable nanoconjugates that efficiently entrapped the drug and sustained its release. The conjugated DTX-loaded NLC slightly enhanced cytotoxicity in NCI-N87 cells at 10 nM compared with the unconjugated counterparts, but not in AGS cells at any concentration tested. Altogether, these findings point to the potential of the developed nanoconjugate in the context of HER2-positive gastric cancer.

articles.title: Engineering a Solid Dispersion-Integrated Fast-Dissolving Oral Film of Nicardipine Hydrochloride for Rapid Delivery in Hypertensive Urgency.
articles.abstract: Nicardipine hydrochloride (NCH) is considered an ideal treatment for hypertensive crises, particularly for the management of hypertensive urgency. NCH is a BCS class II drug with limited solubility and exhibits significant first-pass metabolism upon oral administration, which increases the daily dosing frequency. Therefore, the study focuses on developing and evaluating an NCH-solid dispersion (NCHSD) loaded oral fast-dissolving film (OSD-ODF) for the treatment of hypertensive urgency. The NCHSD was prepared by the solvent-casting method using PVP K90 as the carrier at a 1:3 drug-to-carrier ratio. The solubility of NCH was increased by a factor of 23. The NCHSD released 86.0 ± 12.6% of the drug within 6 min. A central composite design was employed to optimize OSD-ODF, with HPMC E6 and PEG 400 concentrations as variables and disintegration time, drug content, weight variation, and tensile strength as responses. A fast disintegration and rapid-release profile were achieved for the optimized ODF with a disintegration time of 88 ± 3.14 s and 104.73 ± 2.00% drug release within 1 min. The in vitro cellular study demonstrated cytocompatibility of optimized ODF in Caco-2 and NIH 3T3 cells. The findings of the cellular permeability study in Caco-2 cells revealed a significant enhancement of the permeability coefficient (p ≤ 0.05) for optimized ODF, about 9 times greater permeability than pure NCH dispersion. This suggests successful development of NCHSD-loaded optimized ODF with better solubility, fast disintegration, rapid release profile, adequate mucoadhesion and biocompatibility. The findings of this work conclude that the prepared OSD-ODF holds excellent potential and is safe for the treatment of hypertensive urgency.

articles.title: Botulinum neurotoxin type a exposure and executive functioning: A multinational web-based survey.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Botulinum neurotoxin A (BoNT-A) injections have revolutionized both cosmetic and therapeutic interventions, gaining recognition for their positive physical and psychological effects. However, potential psychological correlates and safety concerns have received comparatively less attention. METHODOLOGY: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the association between BoNT-A exposure and executive function (EF) in a global sample. We collected data from participants across 155 countries using an online survey translated into 28 languages and distributed via web-based platforms. Chi-square tests and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) were employed to assess bivariate associations, while multivariable linear regression models using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) were employed to examine the association between BoNT-A exposure and EF scores, accounting for within-country clustering across the 155 countries while adjusting for sociodemographic and behavioral confounders. RESULTS: A total of 46,611 participants were screened, of whom 1,088 were excluded based on predefined criteria, leaving a primary eligible analytic cohort of N = 45,523. Among BoNT-A recipients, Self-Organization/Problem-Solving deficit scores varied significantly by injection frequency (p = 0.008), with the annual-injection group reporting a slightly higher mean score (42.3 ± 12.9), indicating a higher level of reported difficulties in this domain compared to other groups. However, the magnitude of this difference was small. No, clinically or statistically significant differences were observed across the remaining four executive function subscales (p > 0.05). In adjusted multivariable linear regression analysis controlling for sociodemographic and behavioral factors, BoNT-A injection was very small, albeit statistically significant, positive associations with higher scores for Self-Control/Inhibition (β = 0.508, 95% CI: 0.131-0.886, p = 0.008), self-regulation of emotion (β = 0.508, 95% CI: 0.238-0.778, p < 0.001), and Self-Motivation (β = 0.226, 95% CI: 0.023-0.428, p = 0.028), whereas no significant association was observed with Self-Organization/Problem-Solving, and self-management of time. Sensitivity analyses yielded a largely similar pattern across most domains but showed attenuation and loss of statistical significance for the Self-Organization/Problem-Solving association, highlighting domain-specific variability and the modest magnitude of the original estimate. CONCLUSION: These cross-sectional findings identify subtle, domain-specific observational associations. Because the Self-Organization/Problem-Solving association was attenuated in sensitivity analyses and residual confounding by indication is possible, these results should not be interpreted as evidence of toxin-induced neurocognitive changes or a causal effect. Prospective longitudinal cohort studies that incorporate comprehensive assessments of clinical indications and other potential confounders are warranted to further investigate these associations.

articles.title: Tetrandrine potentiated apoptosis and mitophagy to overcome Adriamycin resistance in MCF-7/Adr cells by regulating the Hippo pathway.
articles.abstract: 1.Breast cancer ranks among the most prevalent malignant tumors worldwide, characterized by high rates of morbidity and mortality.2.Adriamycin (Adr) remains one of the primary treatments for breast cancer; however, its efficacy is often undermined by the development of drug resistance, resulting in treatment failure. Recent studies have highlighted that the combination of natural products with Adr can effectively mitigate side effects and counteract drug resistance.3.In this study, the co-administration of Tetrandrine (Tet) demonstrated a significant reversal of Adr resistance, reduced the IC50 of Adr in MCF-7/Adr cells, downregulated the expression of multi-drug resistance proteins, including P-gp, BCRP, and MRP1, and inhibited the migration of MCF-7/Adr cells.4.Flow cytometry results revealed that Tet markedly enhanced cell apoptosis rates compared to Adr treatment alone. Western blot analysis further indicated that Tet, in combination with Adr, significantly increased the expression of Bax while reduced Bcl-2 levels. Moreover, Tet was found to upregulate Parkin expression and downregulate p62 expression, thereby promoting mitophagy.5.Additional experiments demonstrated that Tet substantially enhanced Hippo pathway activity. Upon inactivating the Hippo pathway using si-SAV1, results showed that suppression of this pathway significantly diminished Tet's effects on Adr resistance, multi-drug resistance protein expression, apoptosis, and mitophagy.6.Taken together, the findings from this research indicate that Tet reverses Adr resistance in MCF-7/Adr cells primarily by enhancing apoptosis and mitophagy, at least partially through modulation of Hippo pathway activity.

Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling of Fruquintinib and Its Metabolite to Assess Drug-Drug Interaction Liability as an Object or Precipitant.
articles.abstract: Fruquintinib is approved, including in the United States and Europe, for previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer, regardless of biomarker status. Using in vitro and clinical data, physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models were developed for fruquintinib and M11, a major metabolite of fruquintinib. The models were applied to evaluate the potential impact of strong/moderate/weak cytochrome P450 (CYP) and 3A4 (CYP3A4) inhibitors and inducers on the pharmacokinetics of fruquintinib and M11. In addition, the PBPK models were applied to evaluate the potential for P-glycoprotein or breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP)-mediated drug-drug interactions, with fruquintinib and M11 as precipitants (inhibitors). The simulations indicated that the changes in plasma exposure of fruquintinib area under the curve (AUC) geometric mean ratio (GMR) during administration with strong/moderate/weak inhibitors of CYP3A4 are negligible (< 1.25), and M11 interactions are weak with strong inhibition. Simulated changes in plasma exposure of fruquintinib in the presence of rifampin (a strong CYP3A4 and moderate CYP2C9 inducer) were > 0.20, but ≤ 0.50 (no significant change in M11). Fruquintinib AUC GMRs were > 0.50, but ≤ 0.80 with moderate CYP3A4 inducers, while the ratio fell between > 0.80 and 1.00 in the presence of weak CYP3A4 inducers. The effects of fruquintinib on the pharmacokinetics of P-glycoprotein or BCRP substrates were not clinically significant. These analyses support avoiding concomitant use of strong, and if possible, moderate CYP3A4 inducers with fruquintinib. In addition, no dose adjustments for fruquintinib are required in the presence of CYP3A4 inhibitors, or for medications that are substrates of P-glycoprotein or BCRP when used concomitantly with fruquintinib.

articles.title: An engineered pneumolysin ΔA146 derivative induces apoptosis in breast cancer cells: an in vitro proof-of-concept for antibody-drug conjugate payload development.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) is frequently undermined by the emergence of resistance to conventional payloads, which predominantly exert their effects through the disruption of intracellular targets such as microtubules or nuclear DNA. In pursuit of therapeutic agents capable of bypassing these established resistance pathways, we turned our attention to the engineered bacterial pore-forming toxin, pneumolysin ΔA146 (PLY ΔA146). To evaluate its intrinsic cytotoxic potential independent of antibody-mediated delivery, we generated a recombinant fusion protein (CPP-PLY ΔA146) for direct cellular assessment. This construct demonstrated proficient cellular internalization into both HER2-positive SK-BR-3 and triple-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines. Subsequent functional analysis revealed a potent and concentration-dependent suppression of cell proliferation, yielding half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC₅₀) of approximately 1.140 µM and 1.433 µM, respectively, after a 72-hour exposure. Mechanistically, the observed cytotoxicity was fundamentally linked to the induction of programmed cell death. This was substantiated by a convergence of evidence: a significant elevation in Annexin V-positive populations, conclusive detection of DNA strand breaks, the cleavage and consequent activation of caspase-8 and caspase-3 along with a corresponding increase in their catalytic activities, a decisive shift in the Bax/Bcl-2 equilibrium toward a pro-apoptotic phenotype. Collectively, these results delineate a defined and efficacious pro-apoptotic mechanism for PLY ΔA146, one that is functionally discrete from the modalities of current ADC mainstays. These results provide an in vitro proof-of-concept for PLY ΔA146 as a potential candidate payload for future ADC development, proposing a strategic avenue to surmount existing limitations and potentially augment the efficacy of targeted oncological interventions.
